podSecurity.description:
PodSecurity — pod-level security settings applied to the pod spec.
Set podSecurity.preset for a named preset or declare individual fields.

	podSecurity:
	  preset: baseline

reconcile.description:
Reconcile: true — also apply this declaration as drift correction on every
reconcile. Equivalent to declaring the same entry under both onCreate and
onReconcile. When false (default), only runs on onCreate (idempotent create).

resources.description:
Resources — CPU and memory requests/limits for the container.
Set resources.preset for a named preset, or resources.requests/limits for
explicit values. Preset and explicit values are mutually exclusive.

	resources:
	  preset: burst

restartPolicy.description:
RestartPolicy — OnFailure (default) or Never. With Never, each retry
starts a new pod and the failed pods are kept, logs included.
Supports template expressions.

schedule.description:
Schedule — cron schedule expression. Required.
Static: "0 * * * *" (every hour)
Dynamic: "{{ .spec.schedule }}"

securityContext.description:
SecurityContext — container-level security settings.
Set securityContext.preset for a named preset (baseline, restricted, hardened)
or declare individual fields. Preset and explicit fields are mutually exclusive.

	securityContext:
	  preset: restricted

serviceAccountName.description:
ServiceAccountName is the name of the ServiceAccount to use to run this pod.
More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/configure-pod-container/configure-service-account/
+optional

startingDeadlineSeconds.description:
StartingDeadlineSeconds — if a scheduled run is missed (e.g. the
controller was down) by more than this many seconds, it is counted as
failed instead of started late. Omit for no deadline.

successfulJobsHistoryLimit.description:
SuccessfulJobsHistoryLimit — number of completed, successful Jobs to
keep around for inspection. Default: 3.

suspend.description:
Suspend — when "true", the schedule stops firing new Jobs; existing runs
are unaffected. Accepts a template expression. Default: "false".

when.description:
When lists conditions that must all pass for this entry to be written; see
Condition. When an entry kept in sync (onReconcile, or reconcile: true)
stops passing, the object it wrote is removed.

as.description:
As is the key under .cross.* where the result is accessible.
  as: database → .cross.database.status.phase
Default: same as Crd.

crd.description:
CRD is the target CRD name (lowercase, matches the map key in spec.crds).
  crd: database

labelSelector.description: LabelSelector keys the blueprint registry by CRD-entry labelSelector for label-based informer lookup.

selector.description: Selector identifies which CR instance to observe.

source.description:
Source is the fallback for cross-binary or cross-cluster observation.
When absent, the informer cache is used (zero API calls).
When set, the endpoint is called when the informer is unavailable.

strategy.description:
Strategy controls what happens when multiple CRs match the selector.
  first (default) — use the first match
  all             — put all matches in .cross.<as>[] (array)
NOT YET IMPLEMENTED

CrossSelector.description: CrossSelector identifies a CR in the target CRD.

name.description:
Name is the CR name to look up. Template expressions supported.
  name: "{{ .metadata.name }}"    → same name as the current CR

namespace.description:
Namespace is the CR namespace. Template expressions supported.
Default: same namespace as the current CR.

CrossSource.description: CrossSource declares how to fetch cross-binary/cluster data for a CRD.

auth.description:
Auth handles both ENV-based token and secret reads for cross: authentication
	auth:
	  secretRef:
		name: cross-secret
		namespace: cross-namespace
		key: password

cacheFor.description:
CacheFor controls how long to cache the result before calling again.
Default: 30s — prevents hammering the endpoint on every evaluation.

endpoint.description:
Endpoint is a fully-qualified URL. If set, Inrun uses it directly
and ignores Host/Protocol/Namespace. Template expressions supported.

host.description:
Host is the base URL of a remote Inrun runtime, e.g.:
  http://inrun-runtime.loader-system:8080
Combined with Type to build the final URL.

namespace.description:
Namespace overrides the CR namespace when building info/events URLs.
Optional — defaults to the CR's own namespace.

protocol.description:
Protocol selects which Inrun-native endpoint to call.
One of: "info", "metrics", "health", "events".
Default: "info".

CustomResourceTemplateSource.description: CustomResourceTemplateSource declares one arbitrary Kubernetes resource — any Kind not covered by one of Inrun's built-in resource types (a third-party CRD such as cert-manager's Certificate, or your own CRD).

apiVersion.description:
APIVersion — the group/version of the target resource, e.g. "cert-manager.io/v1".
Required.

crdFile.description:
CRDFile — the child kind's CRD manifest, relative to the Blueprint. At
load it fills apiVersion, kind and metadata.namespaced (declared values
must match), and inrun validate checks spec against the CRD's schema.

forEach.description:
ForEach declares dynamic expansion over a list field.
When set, one source declaration becomes N declarations — one per list element.
.item and .<as> are available in template expressions within this declaration.

	forEach:
	  field: spec.regions
	  as: region

forceConflict.description:
ForceConflict, when true, sets Force: true when applying this resource,
taking ownership of conflicting fields instead of returning a conflict error.
Overrides the CRD-level ForceConflict setting.

kind.description: Kind — the target resource's Kind, e.g. "Certificate". Required.

metadata.description:
Metadata — name, namespace, labels, and annotations for the resource.
name is required. namespace is required for namespaced CRDs and must be
omitted for cluster-scoped ones; Inrun determines the correct scope
via discovery unless namespaced is set explicitly.

	metadata:
	  name: "{{ .metadata.name }}-tls"
	  namespace: "{{ .metadata.namespace }}"
	  labels:
	    app: "{{ .metadata.name }}"

observe.description:
Observe — false: never read this object back into .children, saving
a read on every reconcile; the parent then can't see it. Default: read.

or.description: Or lists conditions of which at least one must pass, alongside When.

reconcile.description:
Reconcile: true — also apply this declaration as drift correction on every
reconcile. Equivalent to declaring the same entry under both onCreate and
onReconcile. When false (default), only runs on onCreate (idempotent create).

spec.description:
Spec is the conventional spec block for CRDs. It is schema-agnostic and
may contain templated values. Only template syntax is validated by
Inrun; structural/schema validation is deferred to the API server.

when.description:
When lists conditions that must all pass for this entry to be written; see
Condition. When an entry kept in sync (onReconcile, or reconcile: true)
stops passing, the object it wrote is removed.

DayOfWeekCondition.description: DayOfWeekCondition declares which days the condition is active.

in.description: In — active on these days. Full English names: Monday, Tuesday, etc.

notIn.description: NotIn — active on all days except these.

weekday.description: Weekday — active Mon–Fri. Shorthand for in: [Monday..Friday].

weekend.description: Weekend — active Sat–Sun. Shorthand for in: [Saturday, Sunday].

cleanupOnShutdown.description:
CleanupOnShutdown controls whether Deletion protection webhook is deleted on graceful shutdown.
Default: false — Deletion protection webhook persists across restarts.

enabled.description:
Enabled controls whether deletion protection is active.
Default: true when the deletionProtection block is declared.

failurePolicy.description:
FailurePolicy controls what the API server does when Inrun is unreachable.
"Fail" — reject the DELETE (recommended for protection; this is the default).
"Ignore" — allow the DELETE through when Inrun cannot be reached.
Default: "Fail".

strictMode.description:
StrictMode controls whether removing the deletion-protection label from a resource
is itself treated as a deletion attempt and blocked.
When true, the only way to remove the label (and thus unprotect a resource) is to
disable strictMode in the Blueprint and restart Inrun Gateway.
Default: false.

DeletionProtectionOverride.description: DeletionProtectionOverride controls per‑CRD behaviour when the global security.deletionProtection.enabled is true.

protectCRD.description:
ProtectCRD determines whether the CRD definition itself (the type)
is protected from deletion. Default true.

protectCRs.description:
ProtectCRs determines whether instances of this CRD are protected
from deletion (via the inrun.dev/deletion-protection label).
Default true.

strictMode.description:
StrictMode controls whether removing the deletion-protection label from a resource
is itself treated as a deletion attempt and blocked.
When true, the only way to remove the label (and thus unprotect a resource) is to
disable strictMode in the Blueprint and restart Inrun Gateway.
Default: blueprint level strictMode.

anyOf.description: DependsOnCondition is the value in the dependsOn map.

condition.description:
Condition — started (the CRD's workers are running) or healthy (running
with no consecutive failures). Default: started.

DependsOnCondition.description: DependsOnCondition is the value in the dependsOn map.

items.description: A CRD name; waits until it has started

DependsOnMap.description: DependsOnMap is the internal representation of all dependsOn formats.

DeploymentTemplateSource.description: DeploymentTemplateSource declares one Deployment to be managed by Inrun.

annotations.description:
Annotations — applied to the Deployment ObjectMeta only.
Annotation values support template expressions.

autoscale.description:
Autoscale declares workload autoscaling behaviour for this Deployment.
When set, the reconciler evaluates scale-up and scale-down conditions on every
reconcile and patches spec.replicas when conditions pass and cooldown has elapsed.
No goroutine — the resync period is the evaluation tick.

	autoscale:
	  min: 2
	  max: 10
	  cooldown: 2m
	  scaleUp:
	    conditions:
	      when:
	        - field: "{{ promAboveThreshold .external.cpu.raw 80 }}"
	          equals: "true"
	    increment: 1
	  scaleDown:
	    conditions:
	      when:
	        - field: "{{ promBelowThreshold .external.cpu.raw 20 }}"
	          equals: "true"
	    decrement: 1

command.description:
Command overrides the container entrypoint command. Each element is a command token.
Supports template expressions.

	command: ["sh", "-c", "echo {{ .spec.greeting }}"]

containers.description:
Containers — the pod's containers, when it runs more than one. With
containers set, image, command, args, port, probes and resources move
into each container, and this entry's env, envFrom, securityContext and
volumeMounts become defaults every container inherits. See Container.

env.description:
Env — environment variables for the primary container, in Kubernetes-native list format.
Each entry has a name and either a value or a valueFrom source.
If omitted, no environment variables are added.

	env:
	  - name: LOG_LEVEL
	    value: info
	  - name: API_KEY
	    valueFrom:
	      secretKeyRef:
	        name: myapp-secrets
	        key: api-key

envFrom.description:
EnvFrom — bulk-load environment variables from Secrets and/or ConfigMaps
into the primary container, in addition to any individual entries in env.
Each secretRef/configMapRef entry names an existing Secret or ConfigMap;
every key in it becomes an environment variable.

	envFrom:
	  secretRef:
	    - name: myapp-secrets
	  configMapRef:
	    - name: myapp-config

forEach.description:
ForEach declares dynamic expansion over a list field.
When set, one source declaration becomes N declarations — one per list element.
.item and .<as> are available in template expressions within this declaration.

	forEach:
	  field: spec.regions
	  as: region
	# then, elsewhere in this same declaration:
	#   name: "{{ .metadata.name }}-{{ .region }}"

forceConflict.description:
ForceConflict, when true, sets Force: true when applying this resource,
taking ownership of conflicting fields instead of returning a conflict error.
Overrides the CRD-level ForceConflict setting.

image.description:
Image — container image. Required (must be declared here or resolvable
from CR). Static: "nginx:1.25". Dynamic: "{{ .spec.image }}".

imagePullSecrets.description:
ImagePullSecrets is an optional list of references to secrets in the same namespace to use
for pulling any of the images used by this PodSpec.
If specified, these secrets will be passed to individual puller implementations for them to use.

initContainers.description:
InitContainers — run in order, each to completion, before the containers
start. They inherit the same defaults; probes are not allowed. See Container.

labels.description:
Labels — applied to the Deployment ObjectMeta and the pod template.
Label values support template expressions.
Inrun always adds: managed-by=inrun, inrun-owner=<cr-name>

name.description:
Name — Deployment and primary container name.
Supports template expressions.
Default when omitted: "{{ .metadata.name }}-deployment"

namespace.description:
Namespace — target namespace for the Deployment.
Default when omitted: "{{ .metadata.namespace }}" (same namespace as the CR).

nodeSelector.description:
NodeSelector is a selector which must be true for the pod to fit on a node.
Selector which must match a node's labels for the pod to be scheduled on that node.
More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/configuration/assign-pod-node/

or.description: Or lists conditions of which at least one must pass, alongside When.

podSecurity.description:
PodSecurity — pod-level security settings applied to the pod spec.
Set podSecurity.preset for a named preset or declare individual fields.

	podSecurity:
	  preset: baseline

	podSecurity:
	  runAsNonRoot: true
	  fsGroup: 1000

port.description:
Port — primary container port as a string. Static: "8080". Dynamic:
"{{ .spec.port }}". Omit to expose no port.

probes.description:
Probes — startup, liveness, and readiness probe configuration.

	probes:
	  liveness:
	    type: http
	    path: /healthz
	    preset: standard
	  readiness:
	    type: tcp
	    preset: fast

protocol.description:
Protocol — network protocol for the container port.
Accepted values: TCP (default), UDP, SCTP.
Omit to use TCP.

reconcile.description:
Reconcile: true — also apply this declaration as drift correction on every
reconcile. Equivalent to declaring the same entry under both onCreate and
onReconcile. When false (default), only runs on onCreate (idempotent create).

replicas.description:
Replicas — number of pod replicas as a string. Static: "3". Dynamic:
"{{ .spec.replicas }}". Default: "1".

resources.description:
Resources — CPU and memory requests/limits for the primary container.
Set resources.preset for a named preset, or resources.requests/limits for
explicit values. Preset and explicit values are mutually exclusive.

	resources:
	  preset: burst

	resources:
	  requests:
	    cpu: 100m
	    memory: 128Mi
	  limits:
	    cpu: 500m
	    memory: 512Mi

rollingUpdate.description:
RollingUpdate — rolling update strategy for this Deployment.
Set rollingUpdate.preset for a named preset (safe, fast, blue-green),
or declare maxSurge/maxUnavailable explicitly.
Preset and explicit fields are mutually exclusive.

	rollingUpdate:
	  preset: safe

	rollingUpdate:
	  maxSurge: "1"
	  maxUnavailable: "0"

securityContext.description:
SecurityContext — container-level security settings.
Set securityContext.preset for a named preset (baseline, restricted, hardened)
or declare individual fields. Preset and explicit fields are mutually exclusive.

	securityContext:
	  preset: restricted

	securityContext:
	  runAsNonRoot: true
	  readOnlyRootFilesystem: true

serviceAccountName.description:
ServiceAccountName is the name of the ServiceAccount to use to run this pod.
More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/configure-pod-container/configure-service-account/

volumeMounts.description:
VolumeMounts — mounts for the primary container. Each entry references a
volume declared in volumes: by name.

	volumeMounts:
	  - name: config
	    mountPath: /etc/myapp
	  - name: cache
	    mountPath: /var/cache/myapp

volumes.description:
Volumes — pod volumes available for mounting into the container.
Supports configMap, secret, emptyDir, persistentVolumeClaim, and hostPath sources.
Volume names support template expressions.

	volumes:
	  - name: config
	    configMap:
	      name: myapp-config
	  - name: cache
	    emptyDir: {}

when.description:
When lists conditions that must all pass for this entry to be written; see
Condition. When an entry kept in sync (onReconcile, or reconcile: true)
stops passing, the object it wrote is removed.

DeprecationTimeline.description: DeprecationTimeline sets the date window for deprecation display.

Duration.description: A duration: Go units (15s, 2m, 1h) or d, w, mo, y

EmitConfig.description: EmitConfig writes the reconciler's conclusions back to the CR and the event stream.

events.description:
Events declares named Kubernetes events emitted in postReconcile.
Map key is the event name — a stable identifier used for deduplication.

status.description: Status declares declarative status fields written after every reconcile.

EmitEventEntry.description: EmitEventEntry declares one named event the runtime emits on behalf of this operator.

message.description:
Message is the human-readable event message. Evaluated as a Go template
against the prepared resolver context.

on.description:
On declares which reconcile outcomes trigger this event.
Valid values: always, success, failure. Defaults to always when empty.

or.description: Or declares OR conditions — any passing condition emits the event.

reason.description: Reason is the event reason field. Supports template expressions.

type.description: Type is the Kubernetes event type. Must be EmitEventTypeNormal or EmitEventTypeWarning.

when.description: When declares AND conditions — all must pass for the event to be emitted.

EndpointsConfig.description: EndpointsConfig controls which HTTP endpoints are exposed by the operator.

enabled.description:
Enabled if false disables all endpoints for this CRD
Default is true

health.description: Health controls whether the /health endpoint is served.

info.description: Info controls whether the /info endpoint is served.

anyOf.description: An enrichment to turn on, always: pods, events, replicasets, ...

or.description: Enrich when at least one condition passes

when.description: Enrich when every condition passes

EnrichTarget.description: EnrichTarget is one enrichment declaration in a CRD's enrich: list.

EventEntry.description: EventEntry declares a Kubernetes Event that should wake this operator.

enqueueGate.description:
EnqueueGate declares conditions evaluated before enqueueing when the event
matches. The Event is the observed object used for admission evaluation.

include.description:
Include is a path (relative to the blueprint file) to a YAML file whose
"watch:" list replaces this entry in-place. When set all other fields on
this entry are ignored. Cleared after expansion.

keyFrom.description:
KeyFrom declares how the matching Event is mapped to primary CR key(s).
When nil the default WatchEntry routing semantics are used.

name.description: Name restricts matching to a single Event by metadata.name.

namespace.description:
Namespace restricts matching to Events in a single namespace.
When empty Events from all namespaces are eligible.

on.description:
On declares which event types trigger the enqueue.
Valid values: ObserveEventCreate, ObserveEventUpdate, ObserveEventDelete.
When empty all three event types are watched.

regarding.description:
Regarding selects the object that the Event is about.
It is a matching constraint only; it does not define primary-key routing.

related.description:
Related optionally selects the object related to the Event.
It is a matching constraint only; it does not define primary-key routing.

type.description: Type matches events.k8s.io/v1 Event.type (for example Normal or Warning).

ExternalAuth.description: ExternalAuth declares how to resolve a credential for an external call.

env.description:
Env reads the credential from a pod environment variable.
Value is the variable name without $: env: MY_TOKEN reads $MY_TOKEN.

header.description:
Header is the HTTP header the credential is injected into.
Default: "Authorization" (produces "Bearer <value>").
Set to "X-Api-Key" or similar for non-Bearer schemes.
HTTP only — ignored by stateful protocol clients.

secretRef.description:
SecretRef reads the credential from a Kubernetes Secret.
Namespace defaults to the operator's own namespace if omitted.
Read via the API server watch cache — no etcd round-trip.

ExternalCallSpec.description: ExternalCallSpec declares one external call to make before resource reconciliation.

auth.description:
Auth declares the credential for this call. For the remote request:
default remote.auth.

body.description:
Body is the request body for POST/PUT/PATCH. Template expressions supported.
  body: '{"name": "{{ .metadata.name }}"}'
HTTP only.

cacheFor.description:
CacheFor gates re-fetch. Calls within this window return the cached result.
Empty: fetch every reconcile. Recommended for stateful protocols where
connection establishment is expensive.

continueOnError.description:
ContinueOnError controls whether a failed call halts reconciliation.
false (default): failure returns an error, halting the reconcile.
true:            failure is logged, result has error set, reconcile continues.

expectedStatus.description:
ExpectedStatus lists the HTTP status codes that count as success, e.g.
[200, 404] for a read where "not found" is an answer. HTTP only.
Default: any status below 400.

fires.description:
Fires controls at which lifecycle points this call executes.
Absent: fires at both admission and reconcile time.
fires.reconcile: false — admission only; reconciler skips this call.

headers.description:
Headers are additional HTTP headers. Values are templates, like url and
body; names are literal. Credentials belong in auth, not here. HTTP only.
  headers:
    X-Tenant: "{{ .metadata.namespace }}"

idempotencyKey.description:
IdempotencyKey controls the key Inrun sends on POST and PATCH so a
retried write is not applied twice. Absent: sent as Idempotency-Key with
a key derived from the CR's UID and the request. HTTP only.
  idempotencyKey: false
  idempotencyKey: {header: PayPal-Request-Id}

include.description:
Include is a path to a YAML file containing a top-level "calls:" list.
When set, this entry is replaced in-place by the listed calls.
Resolved relative to the blueprint file's directory. Cleared after expansion.

method.description:
Method is the HTTP method. Default: GET for external calls, POST for
the remote request. HTTP only.

name.description:
Name is the identifier used to access the result in template expressions.
  name: health-check → {{ .external.health-check.status }}

or.description: Or — at least one condition must pass, alongside When.

poolSize.description:
PoolSize is the maximum connections maintained per url:.
Only meaningful for stateful protocols (postgres, kafka, redis, nats, mqtt).
Default: 2.

protocol.description:
Protocol identifies the wire protocol. Default (Empty(): HTTP.
  protocol: prometheus
  protocol: redis
  protocol: postgres

query.description:
Query is a protocol-specific instruction executed after connection.
HTTP: unused (use body: for request body).
Prometheus: PromQL expression.
Postgres: SQL query string.
Redis: command and args — "GET mykey", "HGET hash field".
Kafka: "consumer-group/topic" or "@topic" for topic metadata.
NATS: "bucket.key" for KV; stream name for stream info.
MQTT: retained topic to read.

timeout.description:
Timeout is the maximum duration for this call. Format: "5s", "1m",
"500ms". Default: 10s for external calls, remote.timeout for the
remote request.

url.description:
URL is the endpoint or connection string. Template expressions supported.
  url: "{{ .spec.serviceUrl }}/health"
  url: "redis://redis-svc:6379"
For the remote request and finalize: default remote.endpoint.

when.description: When — every condition must pass for the call to be made this pass.

anyOf.description: Path or URL of the file
FileSource represents one file source entry.

auth.description:
Auth — optional authentication for remote sources.
Ignored for local paths.

url.description:
URL or path — the file to load.
May be a local path, an HTTP(S) URL, or an $ENV_VAR reference.

FileSource.description: FileSource represents one file source entry.

FileSourceAuth.description: FileSourceAuth declares how to authenticate when fetching a remote source.

fromEnv.description:
FromEnv — environment variable containing the bearer token or GitHub token.
Used when Type is "bearer" or "github".

passwordFromEnv.description:
PasswordFromEnv — environment variable containing the password.
Used when Type is "basic".

usernameFromEnv.description:
UsernameFromEnv — environment variable containing the username.
Used when Type is "basic".

names.description:
Names are finalizers added to every CR besides Inrun's inrun.dev/cleanup.
The Blueprint-level spec.finalizers are merged in.

remove.description:
Remove strips the finalizers from this CRD's CRs instead of adding them.
Testing only.

timeout.description:
Timeout releases a CR still finalizing this long after its deletion
started: Inrun removes its finalizers even though the reconciler has not
returned without a requeue, and emits a warning. A duration such as "30m"
or "2h"; off unless set. Read it with TimeoutDuration.

FiresConfig.description: FiresConfig controls at which lifecycle points an external call is executed.

reconcile.description:
Reconcile controls whether the call fires at reconcile time.
Default true. Set false for admission-only calls (e.g. image signing checks)
where the admission check is trusted and re-running every reconcile is wasteful.

ForEachSpec.description: ForEachSpec declares dynamic expansion over a list or map field.

as.description:
As is the name used to access the current item in template expressions.
Default: "item" — {{ .item }}
When set: both {{ .item }} and {{ .<as> }} work.
  as: region → {{ .region }} and {{ .item }} both resolve to the current element

field.description:
Field is the dot-notation path to a list or map field on the CR.

List field → one item per element:
  field: spec.regions  → ["us-east-1", "eu-west-1"]
  .item = element value ("us-east-1")

Map field → one item per key (sorted alphabetically):
  field: spec.regions  → {us-east-1: {replicas: 3}, eu-west-1: {replicas: 1}}
  .item = map key ("us-east-1"), .value = map value ({replicas: 3})
  .value.replicas = "3"

GateConditions.description: GateConditions declares when/or conditions and optional external calls shared by both preReconcile gates.

eventAware.description:
EventAware preserves individual events through queue deduplication for this gate.
When true, each event that reaches the reconcile gate is evaluated as a distinct
work item. When false, normal queue coalescing applies and gate evaluation is
state-oriented: multiple events for the same resource may collapse into one
reconciliation.

external.description:
External declares HTTP or gRPC calls made before conditions are evaluated.
Results are injected into the resolver under .external.<name>.* and are
available in when:/or: field expressions.

failPolicy.description:
FailPolicy controls what the gate does when it cannot evaluate its conditions —
for example when an external: call fails or times out.
Defaults to open when omitted.

or.description:
Or declares OR conditions. At least one must be true.
When both When and Or are declared, both must pass.

sentinels.description:
Sentinels declares the event-time values this operator uses in gate conditions.
Declared here as a shorthand instead of when/or conditions. It uses the same
semantics as 'or' conditions since first match passes. Must be a valid subset of
preReconcile.sentinels. Checked first before the conditions. Use when to require
more than one sentinel

when.description: When declares AND conditions. All must be true for the gate to pass.

GatewayAPIConfig.description: APIConfig enables and configures the Gateway Gateway API.

auth.description: Auth configures bearer token authentication for Gateway API requests.

enabled.description:
Enabled activates the Gateway API handlers on the gateway.
When true, the gateway registers POST /api/v1/apply,
GET/DELETE /api/v1/resources/..., and GET /api/v1/schema/... routes.
Default: false.

GatewayClusterConfig.description: GatewayClusterConfig holds the connection details for one registered remote cluster.

caRef.description:
CARef locates a Kubernetes Secret whose data key holds the cluster's CA
certificate (PEM, base64-encoded). Used together with TokenRef to verify
the API server's TLS certificate.
Must be paired with TokenRef. Mutually exclusive with SecretRef.

endpoint.description:
Endpoint is the Kubernetes API server URL for this cluster.
Example: https://prod.internal:6443

insecure.description:
Insecure skips TLS verification when connecting to this cluster.
Only valid with TokenRef (kubeconfig manages TLS settings internally).
Use only in local development — never in production.

secretRef.description:
SecretRef locates a Kubernetes Secret whose data key holds a kubeconfig.
Mutually exclusive with TokenRef + CARef.
The kubeconfig may use any auth method internally (token, client cert,
exec plugin, OIDC). Use this when you already manage kubeconfigs.

tokenRef.description:
TokenRef locates a Kubernetes Secret whose data key holds a bearer token
(typically a service account token) for this cluster.
Must be paired with CARef. Mutually exclusive with SecretRef.
This is the ArgoCD credential pattern — prefer it when you want explicit
least-privilege service account scoping rather than a full kubeconfig.

GatewayClustersConfig.description: GatewayClustersConfig holds the named remote cluster map and an optional include path.

include.description: Path to a file whose clusters: key holds more entries

GatewayConfig.description: GatewayConfig declares how the Inrun gateway is deployed for this Blueprint.

api.description: API enables the CRUD REST surface for CRs on this gateway.

clusters.description:
Clusters registers named remote clusters the gateway may route intents to.
When absent, all intents apply to the local cluster (default behaviour).
Keys are cluster names referenced by serve.cluster and target.cluster.
Supports an optional "include:" key at the clusters level — same pattern
as gateway.webhooks.include and gateway.api.auth.include.

enabled.description:
Enabled declares whether the gateway should be installed for this blueprint.
When true, this means:
  - Helm installation was done with '--set gateway.enabled=true'
  - The runtime expects a gateway to exist
Default: false.

endpoint.description:
Endpoint is the HTTP base URL of the gateway, used by the runtime to locate it.
Leave empty in standalone deployments.

standalone.description:
Standalone declares that this Blueprint is deployed as a gateway-only installation
with no companion runtime operator. When true:
  - gatewayEndpoint validation is skipped (the gateway is self-contained)
  - spec: may be empty (no CRDs required)
Default: false.

GitHubOIDC.description: GitHubOIDC configures authentication via GitHub Actions OIDC tokens.

allow.description: Allow — the claims a token must carry. Each one set must match exactly.

GitHubOIDCClaims.description: GitHubOIDCClaims declares which GitHub-issued claims must match.

environment.description: Environment — the environment claim: the job's deployment environment.

repository.description: Repository — the repository claim, owner/name, e.g. "intentd/inrun".

workflow.description: Workflow — the workflow claim: the workflow's name.

GitLabOIDC.description: GitLabOIDC configures authentication via GitLab CI OIDC tokens.

allow.description: Allow — the claims a token must carry. Each one set must match exactly.

GitLabOIDCClaims.description: GitLabOIDCClaims declares which GitLab-issued claims must match.

environment.description: Environment — the environment claim: the job's environment.

namespacePath.description: NamespacePath — the namespace_path claim: the group or user, e.g. "myorg".

refProtected.description: RefProtected — the ref_protected claim: "true" for a protected branch or tag.

HPATemplateSource.description: HPATemplateSource declares one HorizontalPodAutoscaler to be managed by Inrun.

behavior.description:
Behavior — scale-up and scale-down behavior configuration.
Set preset for a complete preset, or configure scaleUp/scaleDown explicitly.
Preset and explicit fields are mutually exclusive.

	behavior:
	  preset: web

	behavior:
	  scaleUp:
	    stabilizationWindowSeconds: 0
	  scaleDown:
	    stabilizationWindowSeconds: 300

forEach.description:
ForEach declares dynamic expansion over a list field.
When set, one source declaration becomes N declarations — one per list element.
.item and .<as> are available in template expressions within this declaration.

	forEach:
	  field: spec.services
	  as: item

forceConflict.description:
ForceConflict, when true, sets Force: true when applying this resource,
taking ownership of conflicting fields instead of returning a conflict error.
Overrides the CRD-level ForceConflict setting.

labels.description: Labels applied to HPA metadata. Values support template expressions.

maxReplicas.description: MaxReplicas — maximum replica count as a string. Supports template expressions.

minReplicas.description: MinReplicas — minimum replica count as a string. Supports template expressions.

name.description: Name — HPA resource name. Default: "{{ .metadata.name }}-hpa"

namespace.description: Namespace — target namespace. Default: CR namespace.

or.description: Or lists conditions of which at least one must pass, alongside When.

reconcile.description:
Reconcile: true — also apply this declaration as drift correction on every
reconcile. Equivalent to declaring the same entry under both onCreate and
onReconcile. When false (default), only runs on onCreate (idempotent create).

scaleTargetRef.description:
ScaleTargetRef — the target workload this HPA scales.
Supports Deployment, ReplicaSet, StatefulSet, or any scalable resource.
Supports template expressions: "{{ .metadata.name }}"

	scaleTargetRef:
	  apiVersion: apps/v1
	  kind: Deployment
	  name: "{{ .metadata.name }}-deployment"

targetCPUUtilizationPercentage.description:
TargetCPUUtilizationPercentage — CPU utilization target (0-100). Supports templates.
When behavior.preset is set and this field is empty, the preset provides the default.

when.description:
When lists conditions that must all pass for this entry to be written; see
Condition. When an entry kept in sync (onReconcile, or reconcile: true)
stops passing, the object it wrote is removed.

HelmSource.description: HelmSource declares a Helm chart that produces Blueprint CRD definitions.

chart.description:
Chart — chart name within the repository.
e.g. "platform-crds"

path.description: Path — chart path within git repo

valueFiles.description:
ValueFiles — list of values files to apply when rendering the chart.
Each entry can be a local path or a remote URL.
Supports environment variable references: $MY_VALUES_FILE
Applied in order — later files override earlier ones (same as helm -f).

values.description:
Values — inline key-value pairs applied after valueFiles.
Same as helm --set key=value.

version.description:
Version — chart version to use. Required for reproducibility.
And also used as git ref
e.g. "1.2.0"

HookDeclaration.description: HookDeclaration declares where a Go hook function lives.

alias.description:
Alias — the import alias in generated code. Default: derived from
location.

fetch.description: Fetch: when true, inrun generate runs go get <location>@<version>.

function.description: Function — the function returning the hooks, func() domain.AnyReconcileHooks.

location.description: Location — the Go import path of the package that holds the function.

runHooksFirst.description: RunHooksFirst: when true, the hook runs before declarative templates (hybrid pattern).

version.description: Version — the module version inrun generate fetches when fetch is true.

HookTemplates.description: HookTemplates declares the child resources Inrun manages at a lifecycle event.

clusterRoleBindings.description: ClusterRoleBindings declared by this block. Cluster-scoped.

clusterRoles.description: ClusterRoles declared by this block. Cluster-scoped.

configMaps.description: ConfigMaps declared by this block, or copied from another namespace.

custom.description: Custom resources of any kind, another Inrun CRD's included, declared by this block.

deployments.description: Deployments declared by this block, one entry per object.

external.description:
External declares HTTP calls to make before resource creation.
Results available as .external.<n>.status, .body, .error

groups.description:
Groups declares sequential deletion stages for ordered deletes.
Each element is a full HookTemplates block whose resources are deleted
as a unit. Inrun deletes stage N, waits until all resources are gone,
then deletes stage N+1. Omit when Ordered is false.
When Ordered is true and Groups is empty, the flat resource fields above
(Jobs, Deployments, …) are treated as a single implicit group.

jobs.description:
Jobs declared by this block. In onDelete, Inrun waits for each Job to
finish, up to onDelete's timeout (default 5m), before releasing the CR.

limitRanges.description: LimitRanges declared by this block, or copied into other namespaces.

name.description:
Name is an optional identifier for this block, used in logs and events.
When set on groups inside ordered deletion, names must be unique across the group list.

namespaces.description: Namespaces declared by this block. Cluster-scoped.

networkPolicies.description: NetworkPolicies declared by this block, or copied into other namespaces.

or.description:
Or declares conditions where at least one must be true for this block to execute.
Works alongside When: block runs if When passes OR any Or condition passes.

ordered.description:
Ordered controls whether deletion happens sequentially with verification.
true  — delete groups in order, verify each is gone before proceeding
false — the default: children go with the CR all at once, by owner
        reference, or by their owner-uid label in other namespaces

persistentVolumes.description: PersistentVolumes declared by this block. Cluster-scoped.

resourceQuotas.description: ResourceQuotas declared by this block, or copied into other namespaces.

secrets.description: Secrets declared by this block: created, generated, or copied from another namespace.

timeout.description:
Timeout is the maximum time to wait for each deletion group to complete.
Defaults to 5m when Ordered is true. Ignored when Ordered is false.

when.description:
When declares conditions that must all be true for this block to execute.
AND semantics — all conditions must pass. Evaluated before any resource in the block runs.

anyOf.description: IdempotencyKeyConfig overrides the idempotency key Inrun sends on POST and PATCH.

header.description: Header is the header name. Default: Idempotency-Key.

value.description:
Value is a template for the key, for an API with its own key format.
Default: derived from the CR's UID, the method, the URL and the body.

IdempotencyKeyConfig.description: IdempotencyKeyConfig overrides the idempotency key Inrun sends on POST and PATCH.

Info.description: Info holds non‑fatal validation messages for this CRD.

IngressTLSSpec.description: IngressTLSSpec configures TLS for an Ingress resource.

create.description: Create — when true, create a TLS secret and populate ingress.spec.tls.

hosts.description:
Hosts — list of hostnames to include in the TLS certificate SANs.
Each element supports template expressions.

secretName.description:
SecretName — name of the TLS secret. Supports template expressions.
Default: "{{ .metadata.name }}-tls"

IngressTemplateSource.description: IngressTemplateSource declares one Ingress to be managed by Inrun.

annotations.description: Annotations applied to Ingress metadata. Values support template expressions.

className.description: IngressClass — Ingress class name (nginx, traefik, etc.). Optional.

forEach.description:
ForEach declares dynamic expansion over a list field.
When set, one source declaration becomes N declarations — one per list element.
.item and .<as> are available in template expressions within this declaration.

	forEach:
	  field: spec.regions
	  as: region

forceConflict.description:
ForceConflict, when true, sets Force: true when applying this resource,
taking ownership of conflicting fields instead of returning a conflict error.
Overrides the CRD-level ForceConflict setting.

host.description: Host — virtual host name for the Ingress rule.

labels.description: Labels applied to Ingress metadata. Values support template expressions.

name.description: Name — Ingress resource name. Default: "{{ .metadata.name }}-ingress"

namespace.description: Namespace — target namespace. Default: CR namespace.

or.description: Or lists conditions of which at least one must pass, alongside When.

pathType.description:
PathType — Kubernetes IngressPathType: Prefix, Exact, ImplementationSpecific.
Default: Prefix.

reconcile.description:
Reconcile: true — also apply this declaration as drift correction on every
reconcile. Equivalent to declaring the same entry under both onCreate and
onReconcile. When false (default), only runs on onCreate (idempotent create).

serviceName.description: ServiceName — backend Service name this Ingress routes to.

servicePort.description: ServicePort — backend Service port as a string. Supports template expressions.

tls.description:
TLS — optional TLS configuration. When tls.create is true, Inrun
generates a self-signed TLS Secret before creating the Ingress.

	tls:
	  create: true
	  secretName: "{{ .metadata.name }}-tls"
	  hosts:
	    - "{{ .spec.hostname }}"

when.description:
When lists conditions that must all pass for this entry to be written; see
Condition. When an entry kept in sync (onReconcile, or reconcile: true)
stops passing, the object it wrote is removed.

JobTemplateSource.description: JobTemplateSource declares one Job to be run by Inrun.

args.description:
Args — arguments passed to the container command.
Each element supports template expressions independently.

backoffLimit.description:
BackoffLimit — number of Pod restart attempts before the Job is marked Failed.
Default: 3.

command.description:
Command — container entrypoint command.
Each element is resolved independently — template expressions are supported per element.
e.g. ["sh", "-c", "echo cleaning up {{ .metadata.name }}"]

containers.description:
Containers — the pod's containers, when it runs more than one. With
containers set, image, command, args, port, probes and resources move
into each container, and this entry's env, envFrom, securityContext and
volumeMounts become defaults every container inherits. See Container.

forEach.description:
ForEach declares dynamic expansion over a list field.
When set, one source declaration becomes N declarations — one per list element.
.item and .<as> are available in template expressions within this declaration.

	forEach:
	  field: spec.regions
	  as: region

forceConflict.description:
ForceConflict, when true, sets Force: true when applying this resource,
taking ownership of conflicting fields instead of returning a conflict error.
Overrides the CRD-level ForceConflict setting.

imagePullSecrets.description:
ImagePullSecrets is an optional list of references to secrets in the same namespace to use
for pulling any of the images used by this PodSpec.
If specified, these secrets will be passed to individual puller implementations for them to use.

initContainers.description:
InitContainers — run in order, each to completion, before the containers
start. They inherit the same defaults; probes are not allowed. See Container.

labels.description: Labels — applied to Job metadata. Values support template expressions.

name.description:
Name — Job name.
Default when omitted: "{{ .metadata.name }}-job"

namespace.description:
Namespace — target namespace.
Default when omitted: "{{ .metadata.namespace }}"

nodeSelector.description:
NodeSelector is a selector which must be true for the pod to fit on a node.
Selector which must match a node's labels for the pod to be scheduled on that node.
More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/configuration/assign-pod-node/
+optional
+mapType=atomic

or.description: Or lists conditions of which at least one must pass, alongside When.

podSecurity.description:
PodSecurity — pod-level security settings applied to the pod spec.
Set podSecurity.preset for a named preset or declare individual fields.

	podSecurity:
	  preset: baseline

reconcile.description:
Reconcile has no effect on a Job entry. Jobs are always a one-time,
idempotent create — Inrun never re-applies or updates a Job after it
runs, since Jobs are meant to run once to completion. This field exists
for schema consistency with other resource types only.

resources.description:
Resources — CPU and memory requests/limits for the container.
Set resources.preset for a named preset, or resources.requests/limits for
explicit values. Preset and explicit values are mutually exclusive.

	resources:
	  preset: burst

restartPolicy.description:
RestartPolicy — OnFailure (default) or Never. With Never, each retry
starts a new pod and the failed pods are kept, logs included.
Supports template expressions.

securityContext.description:
SecurityContext — container-level security settings.
Set securityContext.preset for a named preset (baseline, restricted, hardened)
or declare individual fields. Preset and explicit fields are mutually exclusive.

	securityContext:
	  preset: restricted

serviceAccountName.description:
ServiceAccountName is the name of the ServiceAccount to use to run this pod.
More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/configure-pod-container/configure-service-account/
+optional

volumeMounts.description:
VolumeMounts — mounts for the primary container.

	volumeMounts:
	  - name: config
	    mountPath: /etc/myapp

volumes.description:
Volumes — pod volumes available for mounting into the container.

	volumes:
	  - name: config
	    configMap:
	      name: myapp-config

when.description:
When lists conditions that must all pass for this Job to be created; see
Condition. A Job is not removed when they stop passing: it runs to completion.

KELFunctionRegistry.description: KELFunctionRegistry holds user-defined functions merged from a Blueprint and its spec.imports Modules.

definitions.description: Definitions — the functions, each a named template expression.

include.description:
Include — a YAML file, relative to this one, whose definitions: list is
added before the definitions here.

LifecycleCompat.description: LifecycleCompat declares which Kubernetes and Inrun versions this pattern has been verified against.

LimitRangeTemplateSource.description: LimitRangeTemplateSource declares one LimitRange to be managed by Inrun.

forEach.description: ForEach — expand this entry once per item in a list or map field.

forceConflict.description:
ForceConflict, when true, sets Force: true when applying this resource,
taking ownership of conflicting fields instead of returning a conflict error.
Overrides the CRD-level ForceConflict setting.

fromLimitRange.description:
FromLimitRange — name of an existing LimitRange to copy from.
When set, Inrun reads this LimitRange at reconcile time and copies its limits.

fromNamespace.description:
FromNamespace — namespace where FromLimitRange lives.
Default: same namespace as the CR.

labels.description: Labels — applied to LimitRange metadata.

limits.description:
Limits — the list of limit range items.
Each item applies to one type: Container, Pod, or PersistentVolumeClaim.

name.description: Name — LimitRange name.

namespace.description:
Namespace — target namespace.
Default: "{{ .metadata.namespace }}"

or.description: Or lists conditions of which at least one must pass, alongside When.

preset.description:
Preset — named LimitRange preset. Expands into a Limits list at reconcile time.
Mutually exclusive with Limits — set one or the other, not both.

reconcile.description: Reconcile: true — sync on every reconcile (drift correction).

toNamespaces.description:
ToNamespaces — create one copy in each listed namespace.
Each element supports template expressions.

when.description:
When lists conditions that must all pass for this entry to be written; see
Condition. When an entry kept in sync (onReconcile, or reconcile: true)
stops passing, the object it wrote is removed.

MigrateSelection.description: MigrateSelection restricts which CRs a migration touches; every set field must match.

name.description: Name — migrate only the CR with this name.

namespaces.description: Namespaces is ignored for cluster-scoped CRDs.

or.description: Or — at least one condition must pass, alongside When.

selector.description: Selector is a Kubernetes label selector.

when.description: When must all pass; Or needs one to pass. CRs that fail are skipped.

ModuleImport.description: ModuleImport declares one Module import inside an operatorBox.

auth.description:
Auth — optional credentials for the registry.
Same auth model as RegistrySource.Auth — resolved from environment variables.

module.description:
Module is the registry URL, file path, or short name.
Same formats as RegistrySource.URL:
  File:  ./postgres/module.yaml
  OCI:   ghcr.io/intentd/registry/postgres@v16
  Git:   https://github.com/myorg/postgres-module@main
@ shorthand encodes the version inline: url@version

oci.description:
OCI — when true, pull the Module artifact via OCI/ORAS protocol.
When false (default), pull via Git (GitHub raw URL, GitLab, or git clone).

version.description:
Version — explicit version (tag, branch, or SHA).
Ignored when @ shorthand is used in Module.
Defaults to "latest" for OCI, "main" for Git.

with.description:
With binds the Module's declared inputs to values.
Values are template expressions evaluated in the CRD's reconcile context.
Required inputs not provided here are a validation error.
Optional inputs not provided use their Module-declared defaults.

MutationConfig.description: MutationConfig holds all mutation rules for a CRD.

external.description:
External declares HTTP calls made before mutation rules are applied.
Results are available in rule field:, default:, and override: expressions.
At admission time: all entries fire.
At reconcile time: only entries with fires.reconcile != false fire.

include.description:
Include is a path (relative to the blueprint file) to a YAML file whose
top-level value is a list of MutationRule entries. Expanded at load
time — included rules come first, inline rules append after.

mutateFirst.description:
MutateFirst — when true, mutation runs before validation at reconcile
time. Default true (mutate first, then validate valid objects).

At admission time, mutation always runs first — this mirrors the
Kubernetes webhook ordering (MutatingWebhookConfiguration fires before
ValidatingWebhookConfiguration). This field only affects reconcile ordering.

default.description:

value they held before normalization. The changes are available in status
field templates under ._normalizeChanges as a list of {field, from, to}.

Example:

  normalize:
    audit: true
    spec:
      environment: '{{ default "production" .spec.environment | toLower }}'

    fields:
      - path: normalizeChanges
        value: "{{ toJson ._normalizeChanges }}"

    spec:
      schedule: >
        {{ if typeMap .spec.schedule }}
          {{ cronFromMap .spec.schedule }}
        {{ else }}
          {{ cronNormalize .spec.schedule }}
        {{ end }}

Spec maps a dot-notation field path to a template expression.
The template sees the raw CR (before any normalization of other fields).
Results are coerced to the appropriate Go type via YAML parsing:
  "3"     → int
  "true"  → bool

Empty result ("") sets the field to empty string — not nil.

type instead of being inferred via YAML parsing. This is more precise:

    rather than an empty string, which would fail integer/boolean schema validation.
  - "0" declared as bool → false, not int64(0).
  - "false" declared as bool → false even when YAML would parse it correctly.

Accepted type values: "int", "integer", "bool", "boolean", "float", "number", "string".

Example:

  normalize:
    spec:
      replicas: "{{ default 1 .spec.replicas }}"
      suspend:  "{{ default false .spec.suspend }}"
    types:
      replicas: int
      suspend:  bool

OnCreate — resources written once, when a child is first created; an
existing one is left as it is, unless its entry sets reconcile: true.

onDelete.description:
OnDelete — what runs while the CR is being deleted, before Inrun
releases it: cleanup Jobs, or ordered deletion groups.

onReconcile.description: OnReconcile — resources written on every reconcile, correcting drift.

or.description: Or — at least one condition must pass, alongside When.

preset.description:
Preset is a named tuning preset. Built-ins: high-throughput, conservative, development.
Inline Workers/Resync/Queue override the preset.

prune.description:
Prune deletes children the reconciler applied on an earlier reconcile
but no longer returns. Off unless prune.enabled is true. Used by hooks,
constructor and remote reconcilers; rejected on declarative-only CRDs.

queue.description:
Queue — this CRD's work queue: shared or its own, type, maximum depth,
failure threshold and retry backoff.

remote.description: Remote declares a remote HTTP reconciler. Required when Default: false and no constructor is set.

requeue.description:
Requeue — reconcile again after a delay, optionally only while when/or
pass. A conditional requeue also holds a CR being deleted.

resync.description: Resync is the full re-list interval for the informer cache. 0 → DEFAULT_RESYNC.

when.description:
When and Or decide whether this reconcile happens at all. They are
evaluated first, before reconcile.external, so a skipped reconcile makes
no calls: the CR, functions, presets, the intent and .args are in scope,
but not .external, nor an arg that reads it (rejected by validation). To
decide on a call's result, use preReconcile.reconcileGate. A CR being
deleted is always reconciled.

workers.description: Workers is the number of concurrent reconcile goroutines. 0 → DEFAULT_WORKERS.

ReconcilerPresetDef.description: ReconcilerPresetDef defines a named reconciler tuning preset.

description.description: Description — shown by inrun validate and in the reference.

name.description: Name — what a CRD's reconcile.preset refers to.

queue.description: Queue — work queue settings, as in reconcile.queue.

resync.description: Resync — how often the informer re-lists every CR.

RegistryRef.description: RegistryRef declares how to resolve a specific item from the registry.

branch.description:
Branch — track a branch (e.g. "main", "develop").
The latest commit on the branch is fetched.

sha.description:
SHA — pin to an exact commit hash.
The full or partial SHA works (Git resolves partial SHAs).

version.description:
Version — pin to a release tag (e.g. "v1.2.0", "v2").
Git tags are fetched — version is used as the tag name.

anyOf.description: RegistrySource is one entry in imports.registry.

auth.description:
Auth — optional authentication for the registry.
When empty, requests are unauthenticated.
Auth credentials are resolved from environment variables — never literals.

blueprint.description:
Blueprint — map of blueprint names to their version references.
Key: blueprint name (directory name under registry/blueprints/).
Value: version reference (branch, sha, or version tag).

oci.description:
OCI — when true, pull the pattern as an OCI artifact.
When false (default), pull via Git clone or raw file fetch.

OCI artifacts are pulled using the ORAS protocol.
GitHub and GitLab URLs with oci: false use raw file HTTP — no clone needed.
Other Git URLs with oci: false use git clone.

url.description:
URL — the registry URL.

Git:  https://github.com/myorg/inrun-registry
OCI:  ghcr.io/intentd/registry/postgres

Shorthand — embed version with @:
  ghcr.io/intentd/registry/postgres@v14
  https://github.com/myorg/registry@main

When @ is present, Version field is ignored.

useStack.description:
UseStack — when true, load stack.yaml from the pulled pattern.
When false (default), load blueprint.yaml.

Exactly one file is loaded — not both.

UseStack: false (default)
  Use this when you want the CRD definitions and will override them
  inline in your own Stack. This is the common case.

UseStack: true
  Use this when you want to accept the upstream operator's full
  source tree as-is — their sources, their defaults, everything.
  Useful for internal teams with a canonical registry where the
  upstream Stack is exactly what you want to run.

Warning: loading a Stack from a registry source means that
Stack's own sources are also resolved. A Stack that sources
other Blueprints will pull those too. Understand the upstream
dependency tree before enabling this.

version.description:
Version — the version, tag, branch, or SHA to pull.

For OCI:  semantic version tag    "v14", "v14.2.0"
For Git:  branch, tag, or SHA     "main", "v1.0.0", "abc123"

Ignored when URL contains @.
Defaults to "main" for Git, "latest" for OCI when not set.

RegistrySource.description: RegistrySource is one entry in imports.registry.

RemoteReconcilerDeclaration.description: RemoteReconcilerDeclaration declares a remote HTTP reconciler.

auth.description: Auth declares the credential for the outbound request. Uses the same shape as ExternalCallSpec.

endpoint.description:
Endpoint is the URL the request body is POSTed to. Required.
Template expressions are supported and evaluated per-reconcile against the CR's resolver context:
e.g. "http://{{ .metadata.namespace }}-svc.svc.cluster.local/reconcile"

protocol.description: Protocol is the wire protocol. Default http; grpc reserved.

request.description:
Request controls the outbound request: what the body carries, or the
service's own method and body.

response.description:
Response maps the service's own response onto the reconcile. Without it
the service answers in Inrun's Result. With it the service answers in its
own shape: expectedStatus says what success is, status and requeue are
rendered with the response in scope as .response, and the CRD's templates
run after the call. One call per reconcile either way.

timeout.description: Timeout caps the round-trip. Defaults to 30s when omitted.

RemoteRequestChildrenConfig.description: RemoteRequestChildrenConfig controls which child resources are sent in the body's children.

enabled.description:
Enabled controls whether children are injected at all.
Default when omitted: true. Set to false to disable children injection entirely,
useful for reconcilers that never create Kubernetes resources.

exclude.description:
Exclude is a list of dot-notation paths to strip from every injected child object.
Per-resource exclude (in resources.<type>.exclude) takes precedence for that type.
Example: ["metadata.managedFields"]

resources.description:
Resources maps each allowed resource type name to its per-type config.
When omitted or nil: all types declared in managedResources are injected.
When set: only the named types are included; each entry may override the root Exclude list.
Example:
  resources:
    deployment:
      exclude: ["spec.template.metadata.annotations"]
    service: {}

RemoteRequestChildrenResourceConfig.description: RemoteRequestChildrenResourceConfig is the per-resource-type config inside request.children.resources.

exclude.description:
Exclude overrides the root exclude list for this resource type.
When nil: the root Exclude applies. When empty slice: no paths are stripped for this type.

auth.description:
Auth declares the credential for this call. For the remote request:
default remote.auth.

body.description:
Body is the request body for POST/PUT/PATCH. Template expressions supported.
  body: '{"name": "{{ .metadata.name }}"}'
HTTP only.

children.description: Children controls which previously-created child resources are injected into the request.

expectedStatus.description:
ExpectedStatus lists the HTTP status codes that count as success, e.g.
[200, 404] for a read where "not found" is an answer. HTTP only.
Default: any status below 400.

finalize.description:
Finalize is the call made on the finalizing pass, while the CR is being
deleted, in place of the request. It inherits the request's fields
except body (default none), expectedStatus and when/or, which are its
own: for a delete, 404 usually means done. Skipped by its
when/or, the CR is released: there is nothing to clean up. Only with a
mapped response; without it a mapped remote makes no call while
finalizing.

headers.description:
Headers are additional HTTP headers. Values are templates, like url and
body; names are literal. Credentials belong in auth, not here. HTTP only.
  headers:
    X-Tenant: "{{ .metadata.namespace }}"

idempotencyKey.description:
IdempotencyKey controls the key Inrun sends on POST and PATCH so a
retried write is not applied twice. Absent: sent as Idempotency-Key with
a key derived from the CR's UID and the request. HTTP only.
  idempotencyKey: false
  idempotencyKey: {header: PayPal-Request-Id}

method.description:
Method is the HTTP method. Default: GET for external calls, POST for
the remote request. HTTP only.

object.description: Object controls which paths are stripped from the CR object before serialisation.

or.description: Or — at least one condition must pass, alongside When.

timeout.description:
Timeout is the maximum duration for this call. Format: "5s", "1m",
"500ms". Default: 10s for external calls, remote.timeout for the
remote request.

url.description:
URL is the endpoint or connection string. Template expressions supported.
  url: "{{ .spec.serviceUrl }}/health"
  url: "redis://redis-svc:6379"
For the remote request and finalize: default remote.endpoint.

when.description: When — every condition must pass for the call to be made this pass.

RemoteRequestObjectConfig.description: RemoteRequestObjectConfig strips paths from the CR object before it is sent to the reconciler.

exclude.description:
Exclude is a list of dot-notation paths to remove from the object.
Example: ["metadata.managedFields", "metadata.annotations"]

RemoteResponseConfig.description: RemoteResponseConfig maps a service's response onto the reconcile.

requeue.description:
Requeue asks to reconcile again, rendered with .response in scope. Same
shape as reconcile.requeue; with when/or it also holds a CR being deleted.

status.description:
Status writes fields onto the CR's status, rendered with .response in
scope (.response.status, .response.json, …). Same shape as emit.status.

ReplicaSetTemplateSource.description: ReplicaSetTemplateSource declares one ReplicaSet to be managed by Inrun.

annotations.description:
Annotations — applied to the ReplicaSet ObjectMeta only.
Annotation values support template expressions.

autoscale.description: Autoscale declares workload autoscaling behaviour for this ReplicaSet.

containers.description:
Containers — the pod's containers, when it runs more than one. With
containers set, image, command, args, port, probes and resources move
into each container, and this entry's env, envFrom, securityContext and
volumeMounts become defaults every container inherits. See Container.

env.description:
Env — environment variables for the primary container, in Kubernetes-native list format.
Each entry has a name and either a value or a valueFrom source.
If omitted, no environment variables are added.

	env:
	  - name: LOG_LEVEL
	    value: info
	  - name: API_KEY
	    valueFrom:
	      secretKeyRef:
	        name: myapp-secrets
	        key: api-key

envFrom.description:
EnvFrom — bulk-load environment variables from Secrets and/or ConfigMaps
into the primary container, in addition to any individual entries in env.
Each secretRef/configMapRef entry names an existing Secret or ConfigMap;
every key in it becomes an environment variable.

	envFrom:
	  secretRef:
	    - name: myapp-secrets
	  configMapRef:
	    - name: myapp-config

forEach.description: ForEach declares dynamic expansion over a list field.

forceConflict.description:
ForceConflict, when true, sets Force: true when applying this resource,
taking ownership of conflicting fields instead of returning a conflict error.
Overrides the CRD-level ForceConflict setting.

image.description:
Image — container image. Required (must be declared here or resolvable from CR).
Static:  "nginx:1.25"
Dynamic: "{{ .spec.image }}"

imagePullSecrets.description:
ImagePullSecrets is an optional list of references to secrets in the same namespace to use
for pulling any of the images used by this PodSpec.
If specified, these secrets will be passed to individual puller implementations for them to use.

initContainers.description:
InitContainers — run in order, each to completion, before the containers
start. They inherit the same defaults; probes are not allowed. See Container.

labels.description:
Labels — applied to the ReplicaSet ObjectMeta and the pod template.
Label values support template expressions.
Inrun always adds: managed-by=inrun, inrun-owner=<cr-name>

name.description:
Name — ReplicaSet and primary container name.
Supports template expressions.
Default when omitted: "{{ .metadata.name }}-replicaset"

namespace.description:
Namespace — target namespace for the ReplicaSet.
Default when omitted: "{{ .metadata.namespace }}" (same namespace as the CR).

nodeSelector.description:
NodeSelector is a selector which must be true for the pod to fit on a node.
Selector which must match a node's labels for the pod to be scheduled on that node.
More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/configuration/assign-pod-node/
+optional
+mapType=atomic

or.description: Or lists conditions of which at least one must pass, alongside When.

podSecurity.description:
PodSecurity — pod-level security settings applied to the pod spec.
Set podSecurity.preset for a named preset or declare individual fields.

port.description:
Port — primary container port as a string.
Static:  "8080"
Dynamic: "{{ .spec.port }}"
Omit to expose no port.

probes.description: Probes — startup, liveness, and readiness probe configuration.

protocol.description:
Protocol — network protocol for the container port.
Accepted values: TCP (default), UDP, SCTP. Omit to use TCP.

reconcile.description:
Reconcile: true — also apply this declaration as drift correction on every
reconcile. Equivalent to declaring the same entry under both onCreate and
onReconcile. When false (default), only runs on onCreate (idempotent create).

replicas.description:
Replicas — number of pod replicas as a string.
Static:  "3"
Dynamic: "{{ .spec.replicas }}"
Default: "1"

resources.description:
Resources — CPU and memory requests/limits for the primary container.
Set resources.preset for a named preset, or resources.requests/limits for
explicit values. Preset and explicit values are mutually exclusive.

	resources:
	  preset: burst

securityContext.description:
SecurityContext — container-level security settings.
Set securityContext.preset for a named preset (baseline, restricted, hardened)
or declare individual fields. Preset and explicit fields are mutually exclusive.

serviceAccountName.description:
ServiceAccountName is the name of the ServiceAccount to use to run this pod.
More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/configure-pod-container/configure-service-account/
+optional

volumeMounts.description: VolumeMounts — mounts for the primary container.

volumes.description: Volumes — pod volumes available for mounting into the container.

when.description:
When lists conditions that must all pass for this entry to be written; see
Condition. When an entry kept in sync (onReconcile, or reconcile: true)
stops passing, the object it wrote is removed.

RequeueConfig.description: RequeueConfig declares per-object requeue behavior after a successful reconcile.

after.description:
After is a template expression resolving to a Go duration string (e.g. "{{ .spec.checkInterval }}").
Empty means no requeue — wait for the next informer event.

or.description: Or — requeue while at least one condition passes, alongside When.

when.description:
When — requeue only while every condition passes. A requeue with
when/or holds a CR being deleted; one with only after does not.

ResourceQuotaTemplateSource.description: ResourceQuotaTemplateSource declares one ResourceQuota to be managed by Inrun.

forEach.description: ForEach — expand this entry once per item in a list or map field.

forceConflict.description:
ForceConflict, when true, sets Force: true when applying this resource,
taking ownership of conflicting fields instead of returning a conflict error.
Overrides the CRD-level ForceConflict setting.

fromNamespace.description:
FromNamespace — namespace where FromResourceQuota lives.
Default: same namespace as the CR.

fromResourceQuota.description:
FromResourceQuota — name of an existing ResourceQuota to copy from.
When set, Inrun reads this ResourceQuota at reconcile time and copies its hard limits.

hard.description:
Hard — resource limits. Keys are Kubernetes resource names (cpu, memory, pods, etc.).
Values are resource quantities. Supports template expressions.
See: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/policy/resource-quotas/#compute-resource-quota

labels.description: Labels — applied to ResourceQuota metadata.

name.description: Name — ResourceQuota name.

namespace.description:
Namespace — target namespace.
Default: "{{ .metadata.namespace }}"

or.description: Or lists conditions of which at least one must pass, alongside When.

preset.description:
Preset — named resource quota preset. Expands into hard limits.
Allowed values: small, medium, large, xlarge.
Mutually exclusive with Hard — set one or the other, not both.

reconcile.description: Reconcile: true — sync on every reconcile (drift correction).

toNamespaces.description:
ToNamespaces — create one copy in each listed namespace.
Each element supports template expressions.

when.description:
When lists conditions that must all pass for this entry to be written; see
Condition. When an entry kept in sync (onReconcile, or reconcile: true)
stops passing, the object it wrote is removed.

RestrictedNamespaces.description: RestrictedNamespaces holds the set of restricted namespace patterns.

anyOf.description: RetryBackoffConfig is declared under queue.retryBackoff or external[].retryBackoff.

initial.description: Initial is the first backoff delay. Default: 500ms.

max.description: Max caps the delay so it does not grow unboundedly. Default: 30s.

maxAttempts.description: MaxAttempts is the total number of calls including the first. Default: 3.

multiplier.description: Multiplier scales the delay after each attempt. Default: 2.0.

RetryBackoffConfig.description: RetryBackoffConfig is declared under queue.retryBackoff or external[].retryBackoff.

RoleBindingTemplateSource.description: RoleBindingTemplateSource declares one RoleBinding to be managed by Inrun.

forEach.description:
ForEach declares dynamic expansion over a list field.
When set, one source declaration becomes N declarations — one per list element.
.item and .<as> are available in template expressions within this declaration.

	forEach:
	  field: spec.regions
	  as: region

forceConflict.description:
ForceConflict, when true, sets Force: true when applying this resource,
taking ownership of conflicting fields instead of returning a conflict error.
Overrides the CRD-level ForceConflict setting.

labels.description: Labels — applied to RoleBinding metadata. Values support template expressions.

name.description:
Name — RoleBinding name.
Default when omitted: "{{ .metadata.name }}-rolebinding"

namespace.description:
Namespace — target namespace.
Default when omitted: "{{ .metadata.namespace }}"

or.description: Or lists conditions of which at least one must pass, alongside When.

reconcile.description:
Reconcile: true — also apply this declaration as drift correction on every
reconcile. Equivalent to declaring the same entry under both onCreate and
onReconcile. When false (default), only runs on onCreate (idempotent create).

roleRef.description:
RoleRef — the Role or ClusterRole this binding grants. Required.
kind defaults to "Role" when omitted; set it to "ClusterRole" to bind a
cluster-scoped role instead.

	roleRef:
	  name: "{{ .metadata.name }}-role"
	  kind: Role

subjects.description:
Subjects — the users, groups, or ServiceAccounts this binding grants
the role to. Required: at least one subject.

	subjects:
	  - kind: ServiceAccount
	    name: "{{ .metadata.name }}-sa"
	    namespace: "{{ .metadata.namespace }}"

when.description:
When lists conditions that must all pass for this entry to be written; see
Condition. When an entry kept in sync (onReconcile, or reconcile: true)
stops passing, the object it wrote is removed.

RoleRefSpec.description: RoleRefSpec names the Role or ClusterRole a binding grants.

name.description: Name — the Role or ClusterRole to bind.

RoleTemplateSource.description: RoleTemplateSource declares one namespaced Role to be managed by Inrun.

forEach.description:
ForEach declares dynamic expansion over a list field.
When set, one source declaration becomes N declarations — one per list element.
.item and .<as> are available in template expressions within this declaration.

	forEach:
	  field: spec.regions
	  as: region

forceConflict.description:
ForceConflict, when true, sets Force: true when applying this resource,
taking ownership of conflicting fields instead of returning a conflict error.
Overrides the CRD-level ForceConflict setting.

labels.description: Labels — applied to Role metadata. Values support template expressions.

name.description:
Name — Role name.
Default when omitted: "{{ .metadata.name }}-role"

namespace.description:
Namespace — target namespace.
Default when omitted: "{{ .metadata.namespace }}"

or.description: Or lists conditions of which at least one must pass, alongside When.

reconcile.description:
Reconcile: true — also apply this declaration as drift correction on every
reconcile. Equivalent to declaring the same entry under both onCreate and
onReconcile. When false (default), only runs on onCreate (idempotent create).

rules.description:
Rules — the permissions granted by this Role. Required: at least one rule.

	rules:
	  - apiGroups: ["apps"]
	    resources: ["deployments"]
	    verbs: ["get", "list", "watch", "update", "patch"]
	    resourceNames: ["{{ .metadata.name }}"]

when.description:
When lists conditions that must all pass for this entry to be written; see
Condition. When an entry kept in sync (onReconcile, or reconcile: true)
stops passing, the object it wrote is removed.

RuntimeConfig.description: RuntimeConfig governs the operatorBox as a long-lived entity, not a single reconcile cycle.

allowedNamespaces.description: AllowedNamespaces restricts reconciliation to CRs in the named namespaces only.

autoscale.description: Autoscale declares runtime worker/queue/resync overrides driven by conditions.

cleanup.description:
Cleanup declares when to delete the CR after it reaches a terminal state.
Conditions are evaluated before each reconcile; once met, the CR is deleted
when after elapses. The reconciler keeps running during the grace period.
Works for all reconciler types: remote, generic, and typed. Reconcilers can
also request cleanup themselves through Result.Cleanup.

deletionProtection.description: DeletionProtection overrides the global deletion protection policy for this CRD.

finalizers.description:
Finalizers configures the finalizers on this CRD's CRs: extra names, a
finalizing timeout, and removal. Inrun's own inrun.dev/cleanup is always
added and never listed.

ignoreObservedGeneration.description: IgnoreObservedGeneration disables generation-based reconcile skipping for this CRD.

ignoreStatusPatch.description: IgnoreStatusPatch disables the runtime's automatic status patch for this CRD.

restrictedNamespaces.description: RestrictedNamespaces blocks reconciliation for CRs in the named namespaces.

SecretTemplateSource.description: SecretTemplateSource declares one Secret to be managed by Inrun.

data.description:
Data — static key-value entries.
Values are plain strings — template expressions are not supported here.
If you need templated or dynamic values, use a custom Go hook.

forEach.description: ForEach declares dynamic expansion (same as other resource types)

forceConflict.description:
ForceConflict, when true, sets Force: true when applying this resource,
taking ownership of conflicting fields instead of returning a conflict error.
Overrides the CRD-level ForceConflict setting.

fromNamespace.description:
FromNamespace — namespace where FromSecret lives.
Default: same namespace as the CR.

fromSecret.description:
FromSecret — name of an existing Secret to copy data from.
Inrun reads this at reconcile time — copies stay in sync with the source.

labels.description: Labels — applied to Secret metadata. Values support template expressions.

name.description:
Name — Secret name.
Default when omitted: "{{ .metadata.name }}-secret"

namespace.description:
Namespace — target namespace.
Default when omitted: "{{ .metadata.namespace }}"

once.description:
Once — when true, evaluates templates and creates the Secret only if it
does not already exist; every subsequent reconcile is a no-op. Use this
for generated credentials that must stay stable across reconciles, in
combination with random notes such as randomAlphanumeric, randomHex,
and randomBase64. Has no effect when reconcile: true is also set on
this entry, or when the entry is declared under onReconcile —
continuous reconciliation takes precedence over once. Default: false
(standard create/update behavior).

	secrets:
	  - name: "{{ .metadata.name }}-credentials"
	    once: true
	    data:
	      password: "{{ randomAlphanumeric 32 }}"

or.description: Or lists conditions of which at least one must pass, alongside When.

reconcile.description:
Reconcile: true — also apply this declaration as drift correction on every
reconcile. Equivalent to declaring the same entry under both onCreate and
onReconcile. When false (default), only runs on onCreate (idempotent create).

rotateAfter.description:
RotateAfter declares a time-based rotation threshold.
When set alongside once: true, the Secret is recreated when its age
exceeds this duration. The creation time is tracked via the annotation:
  inrun.dev/generated-at: "2026-04-06T08:00:00Z"

Supported formats: 30s, 5m, 12h, 90d, 1y
Days (d) and years (y) are extensions beyond Go's standard duration format.

Example:
  secrets:
    - name: "{{ .metadata.name }}-credentials"
      once: true
      rotateAfter: 90d
      data:
