        password: "{{ randomAlphanumeric 32 }}"

tls.description:
TLS declares self-signed CA and server certificate generation.
When set, the data: block is ignored — the Secret is created as type
kubernetes.io/tls with fields: tls.crt, tls.key, ca.crt

Default Secret name when name is empty: "inrun-tls"
Default validFor when empty: same as rotateAfter, or "1y"

Example:
  secrets:
    - name: "{{ .metadata.name }}-tls"
      once: true
      rotateAfter: 1y
      tls:
        commonName: "{{ .metadata.name }}.{{ .metadata.namespace }}.svc"
        dnsNames:
          - "{{ .metadata.name }}"
          - "{{ .metadata.name }}.{{ .metadata.namespace }}"
          - "{{ .metadata.name }}.{{ .metadata.namespace }}.svc"
          - "{{ .metadata.name }}.{{ .metadata.namespace }}.svc.cluster.local"
        validFor: 1y

toNamespaces.description:
ToNamespaces - a list of target namespaces
Default when omitted: "{{ .metadata.namespace }}"

when.description:
When lists conditions that must all pass for this entry to be written; see
Condition. When an entry kept in sync (onReconcile, or reconcile: true)
stops passing, the object it wrote is removed.

ServeApplyConfig.description: ServeApplyConfig configures apply-time behaviour for a CRD or target.

overrides.description: Overrides contains override settings for apply operations.

ServeApplyOverrides.description: ServeApplyOverrides configures override behaviours for apply operations.

keepPreviousSurface.description:
KeepPreviousSurface, when true, leaves resources created by a prior serve
target alive when the CR switches to a new target. By default (false) the
reconciler deletes orphaned child resources whose serve-target label no
longer matches the CR's active surface.

resourceConflict.description:
ResourceConflict, when true, sets Force: true on every server-side apply
for this CRD — the gateway takes ownership of any conflicting fields
rather than surfacing a conflict error. Equivalent to helm --force-conflict.
Can be overridden per-request with ?overwrite=true regardless of this setting.
Default: false.

targetConflict.description:
TargetConflict, when true, allows callers to change the target/alias
of an existing CR via the ?override=true query parameter.
Default: false — target/alias is immutable after creation.

ServeConfig.description: ServeConfig declares serve exposure settings for a CRD entry.

annotations.description:
Annotations exposes annotation keys as self-service form fields, written to
metadata.annotations on apply. Declare type explicitly — no CRD schema to infer from.

apply.description: Apply configures apply-time behaviour for all targets (fallback).

category.description:
Category is a service-list label used when listing available schemas
via GET /api/v1/schema/. Example: "Compute", "Data", "Security".

clusters.description:
Clusters is the list of cluster names this CRD is allowed to route to.
Each entry is either a static name from gateway.clusters or a template
expression evaluated against the intent at apply time.
When absent, intents apply to the local cluster only.
Every apply fans out to all declared clusters unless a target entry narrows it.

description.description:
Description is a short human-readable summary shown in the service list.
Falls back to the CRD-level description when not set.

enabled.description:
Enabled surfaces this CRD in the Console as a self-service form.
Requires gateway.api.enabled: true on the Blueprint.
Default: false.

fields.description:
Fields provides presentation hints layered on top of the CRD's OpenAPI
schema. Each key matches a field path in spec. Hints are merged with the
schema at GET /api/v1/schema/{kind} time — they do not replace the schema.

ignore.description: Ignore lists spec field names hidden from the serve form.

include.description:
Include is a path (relative to the blueprint file) to a YAML file with a
"fields:" map and/or a "labels:" or "annotations:" block (same shape as the
inline equivalents below). Expanded at load time — the result is merged
into Fields, Labels and Annotations respectively, with inline entries
taking precedence per key.

labels.description:
Labels exposes label keys as self-service form fields, written to
metadata.labels on apply. Declare type explicitly — no CRD schema to infer from.

matchFields.description:
MatchFields is a list of dot-notation field paths that link a full CR
to this target. When a CR contains all the specified fields, it is
automatically routed to this target.

Used to enable target-level controls (tokens, response config, permissions)
for CRs submitted in full CR mode. Without matchFields, full CR mode
bypasses target-level controls.

Each target must have a unique match list. inrun validate enforces this.
At least one match field is recommended when cr mode is disabled.

Maximum: 3 fields

Example:
  matchFields:
    - spec.mealPlan
    - spec.kitchenConfig

modes.description:
Modes controls which apply modes are allowed for this CRD.
Both default to true for backward compatibility.

name.description:
Name is a template expression the Gateway API resolves server-side to
decide the CR's metadata.name — e.g. '{{ repoSlug .spec.repository }}'.
Once set, it always wins over whatever (if anything) the client sent.
Applies regardless of CRD scope (metadata.name exists either way),
but is optional, unlike Namespace below: most CRDs still want the
caller to choose a name (multiple concurrent instances of one repo —
PR previews, ephemeral environments). Set this only when instances are
1:1 with some other identity the caller already supplies (repository,
team) and redeploys should update the same CR in place rather than
create a new one — a stable environment where only the image tag
or few configuration changes between deploys.

When unset, the Gateway API requires the caller to supply metadata.name
and rejects the request with a structured violation if it's empty,
rather than leaving it to the Kubernetes API server's own generic
rejection.

namespace.description:
Namespace is a template expression the Gateway API resolves server-side
to decide which namespace a new CR is created in — e.g. '{{ teamName }}'.
Same resolution mechanics as Name above, but only applies to namespaced
CRDs, and — unlike Name — is required rather than optional: the
Console form and any Gateway API caller never need to render or
submit namespace themselves. A plain literal (no template) is valid
too, for a CRD whose instances always land in one fixed namespace.

Required when the CRD is namespaced (the default) and serve.enabled is
true — see Blueprint.validateServeNamespace. Meaningless, and rejected at
load time, on a cluster-scoped CRD (namespaced: false) — there's no
namespace to resolve into.

This only affects the Gateway API (POST /api/v1/apply). Raw kubectl
callers are unaffected: kubectl always resolves some namespace
client-side before a request reaches the API server (typically
"default"), so there is never a genuinely empty namespace for a
webhook to fill in the way an omitted JSON field lets the Gateway API
detect intent — deliberately not implemented as a mutating webhook
default for that reason.

Resolves into an existing namespace; it does not create one. The
platform team provisions whatever namespace(s) this can resolve to
ahead of time (setup.apply in e2e, real onboarding in production) —
same as a cluster-scoped CRD's onCreate provisioning a namespace as a
child resource is a different, complementary answer to the same
"developer shouldn't have to pick a namespace" problem.

target.description:
Target is the caller-facing identifier for this CRD in the Gateway API.
Accepts a plain string shorthand ("myapp") or a named map of target entries.
In the map form exactly one entry must have primary: true — that entry's key
is the primary target name and all other entries are aliases.
Defaults to the lowercased kind when not set.

title.description:
Title is the human-readable name shown in the Console service list.
Defaults to kind when not set.

tokens.description:
Tokens maps gateway token names to the operations they may perform on this
CRD and, optionally, the namespaces they may access.
When empty, any valid gateway token may perform any operation on this CRD.
inrun validate confirms every token name here matches an entry in gateway.api.auth.tokens.

view.description:
View shapes what callers read back from the gateway: a payload, paths
left out, and when polling is done. Evaluated at request time against the
fetched CR; no additional Kubernetes API calls are made. Without a view
the caller gets the CR unchanged. See ServeView.

ServeFieldConfig.description: ServeFieldConfig holds display hints for one spec field in the serve form.

category.description:
Category is a section heading for visual grouping. Fields sharing a category
are rendered under the same heading. Works with When — if all fields in
a category are hidden, the heading is also hidden.

default.description:
Default — set only if the field is absent or empty.
Supports template expressions. This is used to synthesize mutation rules for this field
 Ignored for Fields entries, which always infer default from the CRD's OpenAPI schema.
Used by `ServeFieldMutationRules`

description.description:
Description is a short human-readable information about the field.
Informational only.

disabled.description:
Disabled, when non-empty, renders the field greyed out with this string
as the reason. The field is excluded from form submission.
Use for maintenance windows or temporarily locked fields.

enum.description: Enum lists valid values when Type == "enum". Required in that case.

hint.description: Hint is descriptive text rendered below the field.

label.description: Label overrides the field name in the rendered form.

migrate.description:
Migrate configures a field-level migration. `inrun migrate` reads the
value at Migrate.From, applies this field's value/values transform,
writes the result to the field's current path and removes Migrate.From.
CRs without Migrate.From are skipped.

or.description:
Or is a list of conditions where at least ONE must be true for the
field to be visible. OR counterpart to When (AND).

order.description:
Order controls position in the rendered form. Lower values appear first.
Fields with no order (0) appear after all explicitly ordered fields —
any number of fields may leave it unset, since 0 means "no preference,"
not a real position.

Not just form layout: allServeFieldRefs sorts by Order to decide
synthesized validation-rule priority too (see RuleViolation.Field /
ValidationResult.DenialMessage — only the first violation is reported
as the headline denial reason), so the field a developer sees first is
also the one whose error they see first when several fail at once.
Two fields on the same CRD sharing a non-zero Order is a load-time
error (see Blueprint.validateServeFieldOrder) for exactly this reason.

override.description:
Override — always set, regardless of current value.
Supports template expressions. This is used to synthesize mutation rules for this field
Ignored for Fields entries, which always infer override from the CRD's OpenAPI schema.
Used by `ServeFieldMutationRules`

path.description:
Path is the dot-notation path in the CRD spec where this field belongs.
Example: "app.repository", "scaling.minReplicas"
When set, the field is mapped to this nested path.
When empty, the field name is used as the path (flat).

placeholder.description: Placeholder is the input placeholder text.

required.description:
Required, when true, marks the field as mandatory in the serve form —
the browser enforces this natively (asterisk on the label, form cannot
be submitted while Empty() — and is also enforced server-side: an
implicit exists validation rule is synthesized automatically at
blueprint load time (see CRDEntry.RequiredServeFieldRules), covering every
client of the Gateway API, not just the Console form. No matching
validation.rules entry needs to be hand-written.

type.description:
Type is the value's type: the console renders the matching input and
sends a value of that type. Declare it for any non-string field, spec
fields included; the API server rejects a "2" for an integer spec field.
Supported: string (default), integer, number, boolean, enum.

value.description:
Value is a template expression that transforms the submitted field value
before writing it to the spec path. The expression has access to:
  .value   — the raw submitted value for this field
  .request — the full raw intent payload (cross-field reads)

When Value is present, its result is written to Path (or the field name
if Path is absent). When absent, the raw submitted value is written as-is.

Value and Values are mutually exclusive.

values.description:
Values is a fanout map from dot-notation spec paths to template expressions.
Use when one submitted field must be split into multiple CR spec fields.

Example — caller submits "image: ghcr.io/myorg/app:v1.2.3"; blueprint fans
it out to image.registry, image.repository, image.tag:

  values:
    image.registry:   '{{ imageRegistry   .value }}'
    image.repository: '{{ imageRepository .value }}'
    image.tag:        '{{ imageTag        .value }}'

All map keys must be dot-notation (contain at least one dot).
Path is ignored when Values is present.
Value and Values are mutually exclusive.

when.description:
When is a list of conditions that must ALL be true for this field to be
visible. Evaluated client-side as the user fills the form. An empty When
means the field is always visible.
Supports: equals, notEquals, time, dayOfWeek, cron, negate — same as
template source when: blocks.

ServeFieldMigrate.description: ServeFieldMigrate holds the schema migration source for a serve field.

from.description: From is the dot-notation spec path where the value currently lives.

cr.description:
CR mode — submit a full Kubernetes CR (apiVersion + kind).
Default: true.

target.description:
Target mode — submit fields with a target identifier.
Default: true.

ServePermissionSet.description: ServePermissionSet declares operations permitted across endpoint classes.

global.description:
Global applies to all endpoint classes that do not declare their own list.
When non-empty, schema and resources must be subsets of this list.

resources.description:
Resources controls access to the resource endpoints.
Falls back to global when empty.

schema.description:
Schema controls access to the schema endpoints.
Falls back to global when empty.

ServePollingConfig.description: ServePollingConfig configures how the poll URL is generated for the Gateway API response.

field.description:
Field is a shortcut for appending ?field=<value> to the default pollUrl.
When set, the default pollUrl is used with ?field= appended.
Example: 'status.phase' → /api/v1/resources/App/default/my-app?field=status.phase

url.description:
URL is the polling endpoint template.
When set, it completely replaces the default derived pollUrl.
Template expressions are evaluated against the CR at request time.
Example: '/api/v2/resources/{{ .kind }}/{{ .namespace }}/{{ .name }}'

ServeTargetConfig.description: ServeTargetConfig is one entry in the serve.target map.

apply.description: Apply configures apply-time behaviour for this specific target.

clusters.description:
Clusters scopes the fan-out for this target to a subset of serve.clusters.
Each entry is either a static name or a template expression resolved at apply time.
When absent, fan-out goes to all of serve.clusters.
Each name must appear in serve.clusters (validated by inrun validate).

enabled.description:
Enabled controls whether this surface is reachable by callers.
nil and true are equivalent — the surface is active.
false hides the entry from callers, the service list, and lookups.
The primary's config authority role is unaffected by Enabled.

fieldSelector.description:
FieldSelector is a map of dot-notation field paths to values.
When a CR matches ALL key-value pairs, it is routed to this target.
This is a selector — like Service → Pod selection.

Each target must have a unique combination of fieldSelectors.
inrun validate enforces this. Max 3 selectors per target.

Example:
  fieldSelector:
    spec.workloadType: app
    spec.environment: staging

include.description:
Include is a path (relative to the blueprint file) to a YAML file with
tokens: and/or config: keys. Inline fields take precedence on merge.

modes.description: Modes controls which apply modes are allowed for this target.

operatorBox.description:
OperatorBox configures reconciliation for this target.
When set, the runtime uses this instead of the CRD-level operatorBox.
When not set, the runtime falls back to the CRD-level operatorBox.

primary.description:
Primary marks this as the primary target entry.
Exactly one entry in the map must be true.
Validated by inrun validate — not enforced at parse time.

tokens.description:
Tokens restricts which gateway tokens may access this surface and with
what permissions. When absent, falls back to serve.tokens (CRD default).

view.description:
View shapes what callers of this target read back. When absent, the
CRD's serve.view applies.

ServeTargetValue.description: ServeTargetValue is the value of serve.target on a CRD entry.

ServeTokenPermissions.description: ServeTokenPermissions declares the access a named token has on a CRD.

namespaces.description:
Namespaces restricts the token to specific namespaces.
Empty means all namespaces. Ignored for cluster-scoped CRDs.

permissions.description:
Permissions declares the operations this token may perform, split by
endpoint class. See ServePermissionSet for the resolution rules.

ServeView.description: ServeView is the view: what the gateway returns to a caller in place of the raw CR (serve.view, or a serve target's view).

exclude.description:
Exclude is a list of dot-notation field paths to strip from the response
after payload is applied.

Static declaration:

	exclude:
	  - metadata.managedFields
	  - status.observedGeneration

Dynamic via template expression in the list:

	exclude:
	  - '{{ toList (getAnnotation . "platform.myorg.io/exclude") }}'

inrun validate catches the case where a path appears in both payload and
exclude — exclude wins, but the conflict is surfaced as a warning.

fullObject.description:
FullObject controls whether the full CR is included in the view before
payload and exclude are applied.

true  (default) — start with the full CR; payload fields are merged in
                  on top, exclude paths are stripped afterward.
false           — start with an empty map; only payload fields appear.

Omitting this field is equivalent to true — existing callers always
receive the full CR unless the platform team explicitly opts out.

payload.description:
Payload is a map of named template expressions added to the response.

Keys become top-level fields in the returned JSON object (alongside
apiVersion, kind, metadata, spec, status when fullObject: true, or as the
sole content when fullObject: false).

Values are Go template expressions evaluated by the full Resolver with
the note FuncMap. Plain strings (no {{ }}) pass through unchanged.
Expressions that fail to resolve or produce "<no value>" are included
as empty strings — the caller can poll until values are populated.

At apply time: .spec, .metadata, labels, and annotations are available.
At GET time:   .status is also available because the runtime has written it.

Example:
  payload:
    phase:      '{{ .status.phase }}'
    serviceURL: 'https://{{ .metadata.name }}.myorg.io'
    nextSteps:  '{{ nextSteps }}'

poll.description:
Poll configures how the pollUrl in the Gateway API response is generated.
When omitted, the default derived pollUrl is used.
See ServePollingConfig for override options.

ServiceAccountTemplateSource.description: ServiceAccountTemplateSource declares one ServiceAccount to be managed by Inrun.

forEach.description:
ForEach declares dynamic expansion over a list field.
When set, one source declaration becomes N declarations — one per list element.
.item and .<as> are available in template expressions within this declaration.

	forEach:
	  field: spec.regions
	  as: region

forceConflict.description:
ForceConflict, when true, sets Force: true when applying this resource,
taking ownership of conflicting fields instead of returning a conflict error.
Overrides the CRD-level ForceConflict setting.

labels.description: Labels — applied to ServiceAccount metadata. Values support template expressions.

name.description:
Name — ServiceAccount name.
Default when omitted: "{{ .metadata.name }}-sa"

namespace.description:
Namespace — target namespace.
Default when omitted: "{{ .metadata.namespace }}"

or.description: Or lists conditions of which at least one must pass, alongside When.

reconcile.description:
Reconcile: true — also apply this declaration as drift correction on every
reconcile. Equivalent to declaring the same entry under both onCreate and
onReconcile. When false (default), only runs on onCreate (idempotent create).

when.description:
When lists conditions that must all pass for this entry to be written; see
Condition. When an entry kept in sync (onReconcile, or reconcile: true)
stops passing, the object it wrote is removed.

ServiceName.description: ServiceName defines the canonical names used to reference a service within Inrun.

gateway.description:
Gateway is the gateway's Service. Every webhook Inrun registers
(deletion and namespace protection, admission, conversion) points at it,
and the generated TLS certificate is issued for it.

runtime.description:
Runtime is the internal service name used by the operator and runtime
components. This is typically the name used for wiring and enrichment.

ServiceTemplateSource.description: ServiceTemplateSource declares one Service to be managed by Inrun.

forEach.description:
ForEach declares dynamic expansion over a list field.
When set, one source declaration becomes N declarations — one per list element.
.item and .<as> are available in template expressions within this declaration.

	forEach:
	  field: spec.regions
	  as: region

forceConflict.description:
ForceConflict, when true, sets Force: true when applying this resource,
taking ownership of conflicting fields instead of returning a conflict error.
Overrides the CRD-level ForceConflict setting.

headless.description:
Headless — when true, the Service is created without a clusterIP (clusterIP: None).
Used primarily for StatefulSets to enable stable network identities and per‑pod DNS:
  <podname>.<service>.<namespace>.svc.cluster.local
Set this to true when the Service is meant to back a StatefulSet or provide
direct pod‑to‑pod addressing rather than load‑balanced traffic.

labels.description: Labels — applied to Service metadata. Values support template expressions.

name.description:
Name — Service name.
Default when omitted: "{{ .metadata.name }}-svc"

namespace.description:
Namespace — target namespace.
Default when omitted: "{{ .metadata.namespace }}"

or.description: Or lists conditions of which at least one must pass, alongside When.

port.description:
Port — Service port as a string.
Static: "80" or Dynamic: "{{ .spec.servicePort }}"

protocol.description:
Protocol defines network protocols supported for things like container ports.
"TCP", "UDP", "SCTP"

reconcile.description:
Reconcile: true — also apply this declaration as drift correction on every
reconcile. Equivalent to declaring the same entry under both onCreate and
onReconcile. When false (default), only runs on onCreate (idempotent create).

selector.description:
Selector filters which pods this service will route traffic to.
Useful in forEach situations where the labels would likely be the same.

	selector:
	  app: "{{ .metadata.name }}"

targetPort.description:
TargetPort — container port the Service routes traffic to.
Static: "8080" or Dynamic: "{{ .spec.containerPort }}"

type.description:
Type — Kubernetes Service type.
Accepted values: ClusterIP, NodePort, LoadBalancer.
Default: ClusterIP.

when.description:
When lists conditions that must all pass for this entry to be written; see
Condition. When an entry kept in sync (onReconcile, or reconcile: true)
stops passing, the object it wrote is removed.

anyOf.description: SetupApplyEntry is a single manifest to kubectl-apply during setup.

path.description: Path is the YAML file path to kubectl-apply.

wait.description: Wait blocks after this apply until all listed resources satisfy their conditions.

SetupApplyEntry.description: SetupApplyEntry is a single manifest to kubectl-apply during setup.

anyOf.description: SetupConfig declares prerequisite resources to apply before Inrun starts.

apply.description:
Apply is an ordered list of manifests to kubectl-apply.
Each entry is either a plain path string or a {path, wait} struct.
Applied first, before helm installs, after the CRD is installed.

helm.description:
Helm is an ordered list of Helm charts to install before Inrun starts.
Executed as helm upgrade --install — not rendered for Blueprint extraction.

wait.description:
Wait blocks until all listed resources exist and satisfy conditions.
Runs after all apply and helm steps. Use per-entry wait for ordered checks.

SetupConfig.description: SetupConfig declares prerequisite resources to apply before Inrun starts.

SetupHelmInstall.description: SetupHelmInstall installs a Helm chart as a real release into the cluster.

chart.description: Chart is the chart name within the repository, or a local path (e.g. ./).

namespace.description: Namespace for the release. Defaults to "default".

release.description: Release is the Helm release name. Defaults to the chart name when empty.

repo.description: Repo is the Helm repository URL. Omit for local chart paths.

valueFiles.description: ValueFiles is an ordered list of values files (local paths or URLs).

values.description: Values are inline key-value overrides, equivalent to helm --set.

version.description: Version pins the chart version. Leave empty for latest or local charts.

wait.description: Wait blocks after this helm install until all listed resources satisfy conditions.

SetupWait.description: SetupWait describes a single resource to wait for before the operator starts.

kind.description: Kind is the Kubernetes resource kind (e.g. Deployment, Secret, Namespace).

name.description: Name is the exact resource name.

namespace.description: Namespace to look in. Omit for cluster-scoped resources.

ready.description: Ready waits for an available/ready condition, not just existence.

timeout.description: Timeout is a Go duration string. Default: "30s".

StackAccept.description: StackAccept is valid only on a Stack.

patterns.description: Patterns — the imported patterns this Stack accepts.

StackAcceptEntry.description: StackAcceptEntry acknowledges the lifecycle state of a single imported pattern.

author.description: Author — the pattern's metadata.author, to tell same-named patterns apart.

name.description: Name — the imported pattern's metadata.name.

StatefulSetTemplateSource.description: StatefulSetTemplateSource declares one StatefulSet to be managed by Inrun.

annotations.description:
Annotations — applied to the StatefulSet ObjectMeta only.
Annotation values support template expressions.

autoscale.description:
Autoscale declares workload autoscaling behaviour for this StatefulSet.
When set, the reconciler evaluates scale-up and scale-down conditions on every
reconcile and patches spec.replicas when conditions pass and cooldown has elapsed.

	autoscale:
	  min: 2
	  max: 10
	  cooldown: 2m
	  scaleUp:
	    conditions:
	      when:
	        - field: "{{ promAboveThreshold .external.cpu.raw 80 }}"
	          equals: "true"
	    increment: 1
	  scaleDown:
	    conditions:
	      when:
	        - field: "{{ promBelowThreshold .external.cpu.raw 20 }}"
	          equals: "true"
	    decrement: 1

containers.description:
Containers — the pod's containers, when it runs more than one. With
containers set, image, command, args, port, probes and resources move
into each container, and this entry's env, envFrom, securityContext and
volumeMounts become defaults every container inherits. See Container.

env.description:
Env — environment variables for the primary container, in Kubernetes-native list format.
Each entry has a name and either a value or a valueFrom source.
If omitted, no environment variables are added.

	env:
	  - name: LOG_LEVEL
	    value: info
	  - name: API_KEY
	    valueFrom:
	      secretKeyRef:
	        name: myapp-secrets
	        key: api-key

envFrom.description:
EnvFrom — bulk-load environment variables from Secrets and/or ConfigMaps
into the primary container, in addition to any individual entries in env.
Each secretRef/configMapRef entry names an existing Secret or ConfigMap;
every key in it becomes an environment variable.

	envFrom:
	  secretRef:
	    - name: myapp-secrets
	  configMapRef:
	    - name: myapp-config

forEach.description:
ForEach declares dynamic expansion over a list field.
When set, one source declaration becomes N declarations — one per list element.
.item and .<as> are available in template expressions within this declaration.

	forEach:
	  field: spec.regions
	  as: region

forceConflict.description:
ForceConflict, when true, sets Force: true when applying this resource,
taking ownership of conflicting fields instead of returning a conflict error.
Overrides the CRD-level ForceConflict setting.

imagePullSecrets.description:
ImagePullSecrets is an optional list of references to secrets in the same namespace to use
for pulling any of the images used by this PodSpec.
If specified, these secrets will be passed to individual puller implementations for them to use.

initContainers.description:
InitContainers — run in order, each to completion, before the containers
start. They inherit the same defaults; probes are not allowed. See Container.

labels.description:
Labels — applied to the StatefulSet ObjectMeta and the pod template.
Label values support template expressions.

name.description: Name — StatefulSet name. Default: "{{ .metadata.name }}".

namespace.description: Namespace — target namespace. Default: CR namespace.

nodeSelector.description:
NodeSelector is a selector which must be true for the pod to fit on a node.
Selector which must match a node's labels for the pod to be scheduled on that node.
More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/configuration/assign-pod-node/
+optional
+mapType=atomic

or.description: Or lists conditions of which at least one must pass, alongside When.

podSecurity.description:
PodSecurity — pod-level security settings applied to the pod spec.
Set podSecurity.preset for a named preset or declare individual fields.

	podSecurity:
	  preset: baseline

port.description: Port — container port. "0" or empty means no port exposed.

probes.description:
Probes — startup, liveness, and readiness probe configuration.

	probes:
	  liveness:
	    type: tcp
	    preset: standard

protocol.description:
Protocol — network protocol for the container port.
Accepted values: TCP (default), UDP, SCTP. Omit to use TCP.

reconcile.description:
Reconcile: true — also apply this declaration as drift correction on every
reconcile. Equivalent to declaring the same entry under both onCreate and
onReconcile. When false (default), only runs on onCreate (idempotent create).

replicas.description: Replicas — number of pod replicas. Default: "1".

resources.description:
Resources — CPU and memory requests/limits for the primary container.
Set resources.preset for a named preset, or resources.requests/limits for
explicit values. Preset and explicit values are mutually exclusive.

	resources:
	  preset: burst

rollingUpdate.description:
RollingUpdate — rolling update strategy for this StatefulSet.
Set rollingUpdate.preset for a named preset (safe, fast, blue-green),
or declare maxSurge/maxUnavailable explicitly.

	rollingUpdate:
	  preset: safe

securityContext.description:
SecurityContext — container-level security settings.
Set securityContext.preset for a named preset (baseline, restricted, hardened)
or declare individual fields. Preset and explicit fields are mutually exclusive.

	securityContext:
	  preset: restricted

serviceAccountName.description:
ServiceAccountName is the name of the ServiceAccount to use to run this pod.
More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/configure-pod-container/configure-service-account/
+optional

serviceName.description:
ServiceName — name of the headless Service governing the StatefulSet.
Default: same as Name.

volumeClaimTemplates.description:
VolumeClaimTemplates — one or more PVC templates; each pod gets its own volume per entry.

	volumeClaimTemplates:
	  - storageClass: standard
	    storageSize: 10Gi
	    mountPath: /var/lib/postgresql/data

volumeMounts.description:
VolumeMounts — mounts for the primary container.

	volumeMounts:
	  - name: config
	    mountPath: /etc/myapp

volumes.description:
Volumes — pod volumes available for mounting into the container.

	volumes:
	  - name: config
	    configMap:
	      name: myapp-config

when.description:
When lists conditions that must all pass for this entry to be written; see
Condition. When an entry kept in sync (onReconcile, or reconcile: true)
stops passing, the object it wrote is removed.

StatusConfig.description: StatusConfig declares the declarative status behavior for a CRD.

conditions.description:
Conditions — whether to write the standard Ready condition automatically.
Default: true. Set to false to opt out of automatic condition management.
When true, Inrun writes:
  status.conditions[type=Ready]:
    status: "True" | "False"
    reason: ReconcileSucceeded | ReconcileError
    message: "" | "<error message>"
    lastTransitionTime: <now>
  status.observedGeneration: <metadata.generation>

Setting false is rarely needed. Do it only when your CRD's status
schema explicitly forbids a conditions field, or when you manage
conditions entirely via hooks.

fields.description:
Fields — list of status fields to write after every successful reconcile.
Resolved in declaration order. Later fields win on path conflict.

include.description:
Include is a path (relative to the blueprint file) to a YAML file whose
top-level value is a list of StatusFieldSpec entries under a "fields:" key.
Expanded at load time — included fields come first, inline fields append after.

StatusFieldSpec.description: StatusFieldSpec declares one field to write into the CR's status.

clearOnFalse.description:
ClearOnFalse — when true and the when:/or: condition evaluates to false,
the field is explicitly written as "" rather than left untouched.
Use this for transient fields (e.g. crashReason) that should disappear
once the condition that produced them is no longer true.
Has no effect when no when:/or: conditions are declared.

or.description:
Or lists conditions of which at least one must pass, alongside When.
Several entries for the same path, each with its own conditions, make a
small declarative state machine.

path.description:
Path — dot-notation path relative to status.
"phase"            → status.phase
"database.host"    → status.database.host
"ready"            → status.ready

type.description:
Type — optional explicit type for the resolved value.
If omitted, the value is written as a string.

Supported values:
  "string", "str, "" (default)
  "int", "integer"
  "float"
  "bool", "boolean"
  "auto" — infer type from the resolved value

value.description:
Value — the value to write. Supports template expressions.
Resolved against the full CR object map at reconcile time.
Empty string is written as-is — declare a static empty string to clear a field.

SubjectSpec.description: SubjectSpec declares one RBAC subject of a binding.

name.description: Name — the subject's name.

namespace.description: Namespace — the ServiceAccount's namespace. Only for a ServiceAccount.

TLSSpec.description: TLSSpec declares TLS certificate generation for a secret.

commonName.description:
CommonName is the certificate's CN field.
  commonName: "{{ .metadata.name }}.{{ .metadata.namespace }}.svc"

dnsNames.description:
DNSNames are the Subject Alternative Names.
Template expressions supported per entry.

organization.description: Organization is the cert's O field. Default: "inrun"

validFor.description:
ValidFor is the certificate validity period.
Default: same as rotateAfter, or 1y if rotateAfter is not set.
Must be >= rotateAfter to avoid immediate expiry on rotation.

TimeWindow.description: TimeWindow declares a clock-based active window.

after.description: After — active after this time (format: "HH:MM" in 24h).

before.description: Before — active before this time (format: "HH:MM" in 24h).

UserDefinedFunction.description: UserDefinedFunction is a named template expression declared in a Blueprint or Module.

description.description: Description — shown by inrun validate and in the function list.

expression.description:
Expression is a Go template string evaluated by the Resolver.
Built-in functions and other user-defined functions (same Blueprint or imported) are
available inside the expression. The result is always a string.

name.description: Name — how templates call the function.

shadow.description: Shadow: true acknowledges that this function intentionally overrides a built-in.

ValidationConfig.description: ValidationConfig holds all validation rules for a CRD.

external.description:
External declares HTTP calls made before validation rules are evaluated.
Results are available in rule field:, equals:, and message: expressions.
At admission time: all entries fire.
At reconcile time: only entries with fires.reconcile != false fire.

include.description:
Include is a path (relative to the blueprint file) to a YAML file whose
top-level value is a list of ValidationRule entries. Expanded at load
time — included rules come first, inline rules append after.

rules.description:
Rules — evaluated in declaration order.
All rules are evaluated before returning — all violations are reported
together so the user can fix everything in one cycle.

ValidationRule.description: ValidationRule declares one constraint on a CR field.

action.description:
Action — what happens when this rule fails.
deny (default): block at admission, halt at reconcile.
warn: warning at admission, advisory at reconcile.

between.description: Between passes when the field's number is inside an inclusive "min,max" range.

contains.description: Contains passes when the field's value contains this text.

equals.description:
Comparisons: set exactly one.

Equals passes when the field's value is exactly this text.

exists.description: Exists, when true, requires the field to be present and non-empty.

field.description:
Field — dot-notation path to the CR field being validated.
e.g. "spec.image", "metadata.labels.tier", "spec.db.engine"

fires.description:
Fires controls at which lifecycle points this rule is evaluated.
Absent: fires at both admission and reconcile time.
fires.reconcile: false — admission only; reconciler skips this rule.
Example: use for rules that read .intent.* (raw intent), which is only present
at the admission boundary, not during reconcile.

greaterThan.description: GreaterThan passes when the field's number is above this one (strict).

in.description: In passes when the field's value is one of a comma-separated list.

lessThan.description: LessThan passes when the field's number is below this one (strict).

link.description:
Link is the serve.fields, serve.labels or serve.annotations key this
rule is about. Violations report it instead of Field, so a form (the
Console, any Gateway API client) can highlight the input it rendered.
Set it when Field is an expression rather than a plain path, for
example a note call. A literal key, never a template; it must be
declared on the CRD, and linking a plain "spec.<name>" Field is
rejected as redundant. Rules synthesized from required or enum serve
entries set it themselves.

	validation:
	  rules:
	    - field: '{{ isDNS1123Subdomain team }}'
	      link: team
	      equals: "true"
	      message: "team must be a valid DNS subdomain"
	      action: deny

max.description: Max is an inclusive upper bound: the field's number is at most this.

message.description:
Message — shown in the Kubernetes event, webhook response, and operator
log when this rule is violated. Make it actionable.

min.description: Min is an inclusive lower bound: the field's number is at least this.

notBetween.description: NotBetween passes when the field's number is outside an inclusive "min,max" range.

notContains.description: NotContains passes when the field's value does not contain this text.

notEquals.description: NotEquals passes when the field's value is not this text.

notExists.description: NotExists, when true, requires the field to be absent or empty.

notIn.description: NotIn passes when the field's value is none of a comma-separated list.

notPrefix.description: NotPrefix passes when the field's value does not start with this text.

notSuffix.description: NotSuffix passes when the field's value does not end with this text.

or.description:
Or — at least one condition must pass for this rule to be evaluated (OR).
When both When and Or are declared, both blocks must pass.

prefix.description: Prefix passes when the field's value starts with this text.

regex.description: Regex passes when the field's value matches this RE2 pattern.

suffix.description: Suffix passes when the field's value ends with this text.

typeOf.description:
TypeOf passes when the field's value has this type: map, slice,
string, number, bool or null.

unique.description:
Unique, when true, requires that no other instance of the CRD has the
same value at Field.

when.description:
When — all conditions must pass for this rule to be evaluated (AND).
Empty means unconditional.

VaultOIDC.description: VaultOIDC configures authentication via HashiCorp Vault OIDC tokens.

allow.description:
Allow declares which Vault identity claims must match.
All declared (non-Empty() fields must match — unset fields are not checked.

audience.description:
Audience is the expected aud claim value in the Vault-issued token.
When empty, the audience check is skipped.

namespace.description:
Namespace is the Vault namespace to scope the issuer to (Vault Enterprise only).
When set, the effective issuer is {url}/v1/{namespace}.

url.description: URL is the Vault server URL (e.g. https://vault.myorg.io). Required.

VaultOIDCClaims.description: VaultOIDCClaims declares which Vault-issued claims must match.

allow.description:
Allow is a free-form map of additional claim name → required value.
Use for any claims configured via Vault's OIDC provider template.

entityID.description: EntityID is the Vault entity ID (stable UUID for the entity).

entityName.description: EntityName is the Vault entity name (identity/entity name).

namespace.description: Namespace is the Vault namespace the entity belongs to (Enterprise only).

VolumeClaimTemplateSource.description: VolumeClaimTemplateSource declares one PersistentVolumeClaim template for a StatefulSet.

mountPath.description: MountPath — path inside the container to mount this volume. Default: "/data".

name.description: Name — PVC template name. Default: "data".

storageClass.description: StorageClass — storage class to provision from. Required.

Warnings.description: Warnings holds non‑fatal validation messages for this CRD.

WatchEntry.description: WatchEntry declares a secondary Kubernetes resource Inrun should watch.

apiVersion.description:
APIVersion is the Kubernetes API version of the resource to watch.
e.g. "apps/v1", "v1", "networking.k8s.io/v1"

enqueueGate.description:
EnqueueGate declares conditions evaluated before enqueueing when the watch
fires. Sentinels (e.g. generationChanged) are computed against the watched
resource's oldObj / newObj at UpdateFunc time and are valid here.
When nil all events that pass the On filter are enqueued.

include.description:
Include is a path (relative to the blueprint file) to a YAML file whose
"watch:" list replaces this entry in-place. When set all other fields on
this entry are ignored. Cleared after expansion.

index.description:
Index declares field-path indexers that Inrun registers on this watch's
informer. Each entry makes client.List(ctx, &list, client.MatchingFields{name: value})
serve from the cache instead of making a live API call.

 watch:
   - apiVersion: v1
     kind: ConfigMap
     index:
       - name: metadata.ownerRef
         field: ".metadata.ownerReferences[0].name"

keyFrom.description:
KeyFrom overrides the default key resolution (ownerReference → broadcast).
Declare when the standard mechanisms do not express the mapping you need.
When nil the runtime checks ownerReferences first; if none match the primary
CRD it broadcasts to all known primary CRs.

kind.description:
Kind is the Kubernetes Kind of the resource to watch.
e.g. "Deployment", "ConfigMap", "Node"

name.description:
Name restricts the watch to a single named resource.
When set only events for that specific object trigger the enqueue.
Typically used for well-known shared resources (a specific ConfigMap or Secret).

namespace.description:
Namespace restricts the watch to a single namespace.
When empty the watch is cluster-scoped (all namespaces).

on.description:
On declares which event types trigger the enqueue.
Valid values: ObserveEventCreate, ObserveEventUpdate, ObserveEventDelete.
When empty all three event types are watched.

WatchIndex.description: WatchIndex declares one field-path indexer on a watch: entry informer.

field.description: Field is the JSON path to index on (e.g. ".spec.owner", "metadata.labels.app").

name.description: Name is the index name. Must match the key in client.MatchingFields.

WatchKeyFrom.description: WatchKeyFrom overrides the default ownerReference → broadcast key resolution for a watch: entry.

label.description:
Label names a label on the watched object whose value is the primary CR key.
The value must be a valid Kubernetes key: "namespace/name" or bare "name".
Mutually exclusive with Name.

name.description:
Name is a fixed primary CR name to enqueue regardless of which watched
object changed. Use for singleton operators (one CR per cluster).
Mutually exclusive with Label.

namespace.description:
Namespace qualifies Name. Omit for cluster-scoped primary CRDs.
Ignored when Label is set.

WebhooksConfig.description: WebhooksConfig controls global admission webhook settings.

admission.description: Admission controls the ValidatingWebhookConfiguration and MutatingWebhookConfiguration.

cleanupOnShutdown.description:
CleanupOnShutdown controls whether Admission webhook is deleted on graceful shutdown.
Default: false — Admission webhook persists across restarts.

failurePolicy.description:
FailurePolicy controls what the API server does when Inrun is unreachable
for admission calls. "Fail" or "Ignore".
Default: WEBHOOKS_FAILURE_POLICY env / "Ignore".

WorkloadAutoscale.description: WorkloadAutoscale declares autoscaling behaviour for a single Deployment.

cooldown.description:
Cooldown — minimum time between scale events. Prevents oscillation.
Accepts Go duration strings: "30s", "5m", "1h". Default: "1m".

max.description: Max — replica ceiling. Required. Autoscaler never scales above this value.

min.description:
Min — replica floor. Autoscaler never scales below this value.
Default: the resolved value of spec.replicas at reconcile time.

scaleDown.description: ScaleDown declares the conditions and magnitude for a scale-down event.

scaleUp.description: ScaleUp declares the conditions and magnitude for a scale-up event.

WorkloadScaleConditions.description: WorkloadScaleConditions holds the condition blocks for workload autoscale evaluation.

or.description: Or — OR semantics. At least one condition must be true.

when.description: When — AND semantics. All conditions must be true.

WorkloadScaleDirection.description: WorkloadScaleDirection declares conditions and scaling magnitude for one direction.

conditions.description: Conditions — when these pass, the scale event fires (subject to cooldown and min/max).

decrement.description:
Decrement — remove this many replicas per scale-down event (step scaling).
Mutually exclusive with Target.

increment.description:
Increment — add this many replicas per scale-up event (step scaling).
Mutually exclusive with Target.

target.description:
Target — jump to exactly this replica count when conditions are true.
Use for time-based scaling where the desired state is known.
Mutually exclusive with Increment/Decrement.

domain.ManagedResource.description: ManagedResource describes a Kubernetes resource type that a typed extension (either a hook or a constructor) will manage.

apiVersion.description:
APIVersion — group/version, e.g. "db.example.com/v1"; needed for a
custom resource, or set Group and Version.

group.description: Group — the API group, with Version, instead of APIVersion.

kind.description:
Kind — the resource kind, e.g. Deployment. Enough on its own for a
built-in kind.

name.description:
Name — when matching an event's regarding or related object: only this
name. Ignored in managedResources.

namespace.description:
Namespace — when matching an event's regarding or related object: only
this namespace. Ignored in managedResources.

plural.description:
Plural — the resource's plural name, for RBAC, when it can't be
inferred from Kind.

version.description: Version — the API version, with Group, instead of APIVersion.

kubewright.CapabilitiesConfig.description: CapabilitiesConfig is the Linux capabilities to add and drop.

add.description: Add — capabilities to add to the default set.

drop.description: Drop — capabilities to remove; ["ALL"] removes every one.

kubewright.ConfigMapKeyRef.description: ConfigMapKeyRef selects a key of a ConfigMap.

key.description: Key — the key within the ConfigMap.

name.description: Name — the ConfigMap's name.

optional.description: Optional — true: the pod starts even if the ConfigMap or key is missing.

kubewright.ConfigMapVolumeSource.description: ConfigMapVolumeSource is a ConfigMap mounted as a volume.

name.description: Name — the ConfigMap's name.

kubewright.ContainerSecurityContext.description: ContainerSecurityContext is a container's security settings: a preset, or the fields.

allowPrivilegeEscalation.description:
AllowPrivilegeEscalation — false stops a process gaining more privileges
than its parent. Kubernetes default: true.

capabilities.description: Capabilities — Linux capabilities to add and drop.

preset.description:
Preset — baseline, restricted, hardened, or one from the registry.
presets.ExpandContainerSecurity expands it.

readOnlyRootFilesystem.description: ReadOnlyRootFilesystem — true mounts the root filesystem read-only.

runAsGroup.description: RunAsGroup — the group ID the container runs as.

runAsNonRoot.description: RunAsNonRoot — true refuses to run the container as root.

runAsUser.description: RunAsUser — the user ID the container runs as.

kubewright.CustomResourceMetadata.description: CustomResourceMetadata is the metadata a custom resource spec sets.

labels.description: Labels — set on the object.

name.description: Name — the object's name. Required.

namespace.description: Namespace — where to create it. Empty means the owner's.

namespaced.description:
Namespaced — false for a cluster-scoped kind: the object gets no
namespace. nil or true: namespaced.

kubewright.EmptyDirVolumeSource.description: EmptyDirVolumeSource is an empty directory that lives as long as the pod.

kubewright.EnvFrom.description: EnvFrom is the Secrets and ConfigMaps whose keys become environment variables.

configMapRef.description: ConfigMapRef — ConfigMaps whose keys become environment variables.

secretRef.description: SecretRef — Secrets whose keys become environment variables.

kubewright.EnvFromRef.description: EnvFromRef imports the keys of one Secret or ConfigMap as environment variables.

keys.description:
Keys — import only these keys, each as its own variable named
Prefix + key + Suffix. Empty imports every key.

name.description: Name — the Secret or ConfigMap to import.

optional.description: Optional — true: the pod starts even if the source is missing.

prefix.description: Prefix — prepended to each imported variable's name.

suffix.description: Suffix — appended to each imported variable's name. Needs Keys.

name.description: Name — the variable's name.

value.description: Value — a literal value. Set this or ValueFrom.

valueFrom.description: ValueFrom — read the value from a Secret or ConfigMap key.

kubewright.HPABehavior.description: HPABehavior is how fast a HorizontalPodAutoscaler scales up and down: a preset, or ScaleUp and ScaleDown.

preset.description:
Preset — web, api, latency-sensitive, batch, cost-optimized, or one
from the registry. presets.ExpandHPA expands it.

scaleDown.description: ScaleDown — how fast replicas are removed.

scaleUp.description: ScaleUp — how fast replicas are added.

kubewright.HPAScalingPolicy.description: HPAScalingPolicy limits one scaling step per period.

type.description: Type — Pods (a count) or Percent (of current replicas).

value.description: Value — the pods or percent allowed per period.

kubewright.HPAScalingRules.description: HPAScalingRules is one scaling direction, up or down.

policies.description: Policies — the limits on each step; SelectPolicy picks among them.

selectPolicy.description: SelectPolicy — Max, Min or Disabled. Default: Max.

stabilizationWindowSeconds.description:
StabilizationWindowSeconds — how far back to look before acting.
Kubernetes defaults: 300 down, 0 up.

kubewright.HostPathVolumeSource.description: HostPathVolumeSource is a path on the node mounted as a volume.

path.description: Path — the path on the node.

type.description:
Type — what must exist at Path: DirectoryOrCreate, Directory,
FileOrCreate, File, Socket, CharDevice or BlockDevice. Empty checks nothing.

kubewright.Labels.description: Labels is a set of Kubernetes labels or annotations.

kubewright.LimitRangeItem.description: LimitRangeItem is the defaults and bounds for one type of object in a namespace.

default.description: Default — the limits given to a container that sets none.

defaultRequest.description: DefaultRequest — the requests given to a container that sets none.

max.description: Max — the most each resource may be, e.g. {"cpu": "2", "memory": "4Gi"}.

maxLimitRequestRatio.description: MaxLimitRequestRatio — the most a limit may be, as a multiple of its request.

min.description: Min — the least each resource may be.

ports.description: Ports — the ports allowed. Empty allows every port.

to.description: To — the destinations allowed out. Empty allows every destination.

kubewright.NetworkPolicyIPBlock.description: NetworkPolicyIPBlock describes an IP CIDR range.

except.description: Except — ranges inside CIDR to leave out.

from.description: From — the sources allowed in. Empty allows every source.

ports.description: Ports — the ports allowed. Empty allows every port.

kubewright.NetworkPolicyPeer.description: NetworkPolicyPeer selects a set of pods or namespaces.

ipBlock.description: IPBlock — a range of IP addresses.

namespaceSelector.description: NamespaceSelector — namespaces, by label. Empty selects every namespace.

podSelector.description:
PodSelector — pods in the policy's namespace, by label. Empty selects
every pod.

kubewright.NetworkPolicyPort.description: NetworkPolicyPort describes a port allowed by a rule.

port.description: Port — a port number or name.

kubewright.PVCVolumeSource.description: PVCVolumeSource is an existing PersistentVolumeClaim mounted as a volume.

kubewright.PodSecurityContext.description: PodSecurityContext is a pod's security settings: a preset, or the fields.

fsGroup.description: FSGroup — the group that owns the pod's volumes.

preset.description:
Preset — baseline, restricted, hardened, or one from the registry.
presets.ExpandPodSecurity expands it.

runAsGroup.description: RunAsGroup — the group ID every container runs as.

runAsNonRoot.description: RunAsNonRoot — true refuses to run any container as root.

runAsUser.description: RunAsUser — the user ID every container runs as.

kubewright.ProbeConfig.description: ProbeConfig is one probe: an HTTP GET or a TCP connection, with timings from a preset, explicit fields, or both.

failureThreshold.description: FailureThreshold — consecutive failures before the probe counts as failed.

initialDelaySeconds.description: InitialDelaySeconds — delay before the first probe.

path.description: Path — HTTP GET path. Required when type is "http".

port.description: Port — the port to probe. Default: the container's port.

preset.description:
Preset — a named set of timings: fast, standard, patient, slow-start,
or one from the registry. Explicit timings below override it.

successThreshold.description:
SuccessThreshold — consecutive successes before it counts as passed
again. Must be 1 for liveness and startup.

timeoutSeconds.description: TimeoutSeconds — how long one probe may take.

type.description: Type — http or tcp. Default: http when Path is set.

kubewright.ProbesConfig.description: ProbesConfig is a container's startup, liveness and readiness probes.

liveness.description: Liveness — failing it restarts the container.

readiness.description: Readiness — failing it takes the pod out of its Services' endpoints.

startup.description:
Startup — holds off the other probes until the container has started;
failing it restarts the container.

kubewright.ResourceRequirements.description: ResourceRequirements is a container's requests and limits as quantity strings, or a preset that supplies both.

limits.description: Limits — the most the container may use, e.g. {"cpu": "500m", "memory": "512Mi"}.

preset.description:
Preset — a named size (tiny, small, medium, large, …). When set,
Requests and Limits are ignored: the preset supplies both.

kubewright.RollingUpdateBehavior.description: RollingUpdateBehavior is how a rollout replaces pods: a preset, or MaxSurge and MaxUnavailable.

maxSurge.description:
MaxSurge — pods allowed above the desired count, as a count ("1") or a
percentage ("25%").

maxUnavailable.description:
MaxUnavailable — pods allowed to be unavailable, as a count or a
percentage.

preset.description:
Preset — safe, fast, blue-green, or one from the registry.
presets.ExpandRollingUpdate expands it.

apiVersion.description: APIVersion — the target's group and version, e.g. "apps/v1".

kind.description: Kind — the target's kind, e.g. Deployment or StatefulSet.

name.description: Name — the target's name, in the HorizontalPodAutoscaler's namespace.

kubewright.SecretKeyRef.description: SecretKeyRef selects a key of a Secret.

key.description: Key — the key within the Secret.

name.description: Name — the Secret's name.

optional.description: Optional — true: the pod starts even if the Secret or key is missing.

kubewright.SecretVolumeSource.description: SecretVolumeSource is a Secret mounted as a volume.

name.description: Name — the Secret's name.

kubewright.ValueFrom.description: ValueFrom is where an environment variable's value comes from.

configMapKeyRef.description: ConfigMapKeyRef — a key of a ConfigMap in the pod's namespace.

secretKeyRef.description: SecretKeyRef — a key of a Secret in the pod's namespace.

kubewright.VolumeMount.description: VolumeMount mounts a pod volume into a container.

mountPath.description: MountPath — where the volume appears in the container.

name.description: Name — the volume's name.

subPath.description: SubPath — mount only this path within the volume. Empty mounts its root.

configMap.description: ConfigMap — a ConfigMap's keys as files.

emptyDir.description: EmptyDir — an empty directory that lives as long as the pod.

hostPath.description: HostPath — a file or directory on the node.

name.description: Name — the volume's name, which a VolumeMount refers to.

secret.description: Secret — a Secret's keys as files.

presets.ContainerSecurity.description: ContainerSecurity is a named container security context.

allowPrivilegeEscalation.description:
AllowPrivilegeEscalation — false stops a process gaining more privileges
than its parent.

capabilities.description: Capabilities — Linux capabilities to add and drop.

description.description: Description — what the preset is for.

name.description: Name — what a securityContext.preset names to use this preset; names ignore case.

readOnlyRootFilesystem.description: ReadOnlyRootFilesystem — true mounts the container's root filesystem read-only.

runAsGroup.description: RunAsGroup — the group ID the container runs as.

runAsNonRoot.description: RunAsNonRoot — true refuses to start the container as root.

runAsUser.description: RunAsUser — the user ID the container runs as.

presets.HPA.description: HPA is a named HorizontalPodAutoscaler setup: replica bounds, a CPU target and scaling behavior.

behavior.description: Behavior — how fast to scale up and down. Replaces the HPA's behavior.

description.description: Description — what the preset is for.

maxReplicas.description: MaxReplicas — the most pods, used when the HPA sets none.

minReplicas.description: MinReplicas — the fewest pods, used when the HPA sets none.

name.description: Name — what a HorizontalPodAutoscaler's behavior.preset names to use this preset; names ignore case.

targetCPUUtilizationPercentage.description:
TargetCPUUtilizationPercentage — the average CPU use to scale toward,
used when the HPA sets none.

presets.LimitRange.description: LimitRange is a named set of LimitRange items.

description.description: Description — what the preset is for.

limits.description:
Limits — per-container and per-pod defaults and bounds, used when the
LimitRange sets none.

name.description: Name — what a LimitRange names to use this preset; names ignore case.

presets.NetworkPolicy.description: NetworkPolicy is a named set of NetworkPolicy rules.

description.description: Description — what the preset is for.

egress.description: Egress — the rules for traffic out. Replaces the policy's.

ingress.description: Ingress — the rules for traffic in. Replaces the policy's.

name.description: Name — what a NetworkPolicy names to use this preset; names ignore case.

podSelector.description:
PodSelector — the labels of the pods the policy applies to, used when the
policy sets none. An empty map selects every pod.

policyTypes.description: PolicyTypes — Ingress, Egress or both. Replaces the policy's.

presets.PDB.description: PDB is a named PodDisruptionBudget limit: MinAvailable or MaxUnavailable, each a count or a percentage.

description.description: Description — what the preset is for.

maxUnavailable.description: MaxUnavailable — pods that may be down, used when the budget doesn't set it.

minAvailable.description: MinAvailable — pods that must stay up, used when the budget doesn't set it.

name.description: Name — what a PodDisruptionBudget names to use this preset; names ignore case.

presets.PodSecurity.description: PodSecurity is a named pod security context.

description.description: Description — what the preset is for.

fsGroup.description: FSGroup — the group that owns mounted volumes.

name.description: Name — what a podSecurity.preset names to use this preset; names ignore case.

runAsGroup.description: RunAsGroup — the group ID every container runs as.

runAsNonRoot.description: RunAsNonRoot — true refuses to start any container as root.

runAsUser.description: RunAsUser — the user ID every container runs as.

presets.Probe.description: Probe is a named set of probe timings.

description.description: Description — what the preset is for.

failureThreshold.description: FailureThreshold — consecutive failures before the probe counts as failed.

initialDelaySeconds.description: InitialDelaySeconds — wait this long after start before the first probe.

name.description: Name — what a probe's preset names to use this preset; names ignore case.

successThreshold.description: SuccessThreshold — consecutive successes before it counts as passed again.

timeoutSeconds.description: TimeoutSeconds — how long one probe may take.

presets.Resource.description: Resource is a named set of CPU and memory requests and limits.

description.description: Description — what the preset is for.

limits.description: Limits — the most the container may use.

name.description: Name — what a resources.preset names to use this preset; names ignore case.

presets.ResourceQuota.description: ResourceQuota is a named set of a namespace's hard limits.

description.description: Description — what the preset is for.

hard.description:
Hard — the namespace's limits, e.g. {"pods": "10", "requests.cpu": "4"}.
Replaces the quota's.

name.description: Name — what a ResourceQuota names to use this preset; names ignore case.

presets.RollingUpdate.description: RollingUpdate is a named Deployment rolling update strategy.

description.description: Description — what the preset is for.

maxSurge.description: MaxSurge — pods allowed above the desired count during a rollout.

maxUnavailable.description: MaxUnavailable — pods allowed to be unavailable during a rollout.

name.description: Name — what a rollingUpdate.preset names to use this preset; names ignore case.
